output: On April 23, a Russian SU-27 fighter displayed a show of aggression towards a US RC-135U aircraft during a routine mission over the Sea of Okhotsk, reportedly employing threatening maneuvers and exposing air-to-air missiles. This incident occurred amidst ongoing tension between the US and Russia over Russia's involvement in Ukraine, with previous incidents including a Russian fighter jet's low-altitude passes over a US Navy destroyer.

The Prince of Wales, Charles, and his wife Camilla are embarking on a 12-day tour of Australia and New Zealand, marking the 15th time Charles visits Australia, and they will celebrate Charles' 67th birthday with a barbecue in Western Australia.

A 70-year-old woman was attacked in Sneem, County Kerry, on 20 September, and a man has been detained in Killarney in connection with the incident. He is currently being questioned at the local Garda (police) station.

The Medical Practitioners Tribunal decided to erase Hugh McGoldrick's name from the medical register after his false conduct in drug trials on sleep disorder patients, as no appeal was filed before the 28-day deadline passed.

A 21-year-old male is under police investigation after a body was found in a wooded area in Dorking, Surrey, and Surrey Police is waiting for the results of a post-mortem examination to confirm the cause of death and identity of the deceased.

A man identified as Josh Hanson was stabbed and died at the RE bar in Eastcote, Hillingdon. Over 40 people were reportedly at the bar at the time of the attack, and Scotland Yard urges anyone who was there or in the area around 01:00 Sunday to contact them with potential information about the incident, as no arrests have been made yet.

A potential new ferry service between Sandown and Southsea is suggested to increase tourism, with tentative plans for operational days on Tuesdays and Thursdays in July and August, and discussions underway between the Isle of Wight Council and Hovertravel to finalize details and location.

On Sunday at roughly 2 am BST, a 30-year-old man was viciously attacked by around eight individuals on the Heights, with the culprits yet to be identified; a suspect was arrested but released on bail, as police continue to gather information from the public.

In the last two days, the death toll in flood-hit regions of India, particularly Assam, has doubled, with over 100 fatalities and nearly half a million people affected as the monsoon rains continue to wreak havoc across at least 20 states, prompting the government to offer aid and commit to finding a long-term solution for the recurring flooding.

The Premier League's upcoming season opens with Arsenal hosting Leicester City on 11 August, and Sky Sports will broadcast 10 Friday night matches as part of their multi-million pound deal with the Premier League, while a significant third of Premier League football fans admit to regularly watching matches live online via unofficial streams.

Cristian Montano, a former Oldham Athletic midfielder with 48 appearances and 4 goals, was dismissed from the club following an investigation into spot-fixing by the National Crime Agency, with the club stating they took the matter extremely seriously and acted swiftly in making the decision.

A man, Rick Edwards, was sentenced to a suspended jail term and supervision order for setting a small piece of wallpaper on fire at a former Pontins resort in Brixham, which led to a extensive blaze that destroyed the 42-acre site and increased the final cost of demolition due to the damage caused and asbestos removal difficulties.

Footballer Matt Wilson joined Nottingham Forest from Celtic for £2.5m in August 2013 and made 51 appearances during his second spell at the team, having also played for Preston North End and Notts County earlier in his career.

In the second ODI of the five-match series in Colombo, Australia's left-arm seamer-Faulkner finished with 3 wickets (Kusal Perera, Angelo Mathews, Thisara Perera) to restrict Sri Lanka to 288. Australia, in response, were bowled out for 206, with Amila Aponso taking 4 wickets (4-18), including besting Wade's 76. This victory by 82 runs levels the series at 1-1. Bruce Reid, Anthony Stuart, Brett Lee, Clint McKay, and Dan Christian are the other Australians who achieved an ODI hat-trick.

Sale Sharks coach Steve Diamond confirms that Vadim Cobilas, their Moldovan international player, is moving to France's Top 14, and the club is in advanced talks with David Seymour, Will Addison, and Mark Jennings about new deals, with potential departures and recruitment for the next season underway.

India, led by Shikhar Dhawan's 117 and Virat Kohli's 105, were on course to achieve the highest successful run-chase in Australia at 277-1. However, a dramatic collapse left them all out for 323, thanks to Kane Richardson's 5-68, with Australia already 4-0 up in the series, leading to a potential whitewash in the final match in Sydney.

The Hammersmith and City Line and parts of the Circle Line were temporarily suspended due to concerns debris from a fire in a 24-storey block might fall onto the tracks, at the request of the London Fire Brigade, with 58 deaths presumed and potential for higher losses.
Scottish footballer Jamie Hamill, previously of Hearts, has returned to his former club Kilmarnock after signing a three-year contract, set to make his 150th appearance there upon his second debut.

Ipswich fan Ross Morgan accidentally punched a hole in his ceiling while celebrating a goal scored by Paul Anderson during an Ipswich v Norwich match, and Anderson subsequently offered to pay for the repairs as a gesture of goodwill.

In Wales, retailers are now required to keep tobacco products out of public view, a move aimed at reducing the appeal of smoking and improving public health, with violators facing fines and imprisonment.

Lucas, a 20-year-old footballer, is set to join Bristol Rovers' League Two squad for a third time this season, having scored three goals in ten appearances for a previous National League side. His manager suggests that he is a potent threat to defenses and could provide a boost in the forward lines.

Knaresborough station in North Yorkshire is undergoing restoration, including waterproofing and rebuilding of the chimney stack, with night-time work on the platform canopy aimed at minimizing disruptions, as noted by both Network Rail and train operator Northern, who acknowledge the station's historical beauty.

Former NFL player Lawrence Phillips, who was convicted of multiple assaults and served a long prison sentence, is believed to have taken his own life at the age of 40, after being accused of killing his former cellmate and facing a trial for the crime.

The article discusses a proposed extension of bus lane operating hours for the Belfast Rapid Transit (BRT) plan from 7:00 to 19:00, aiming for clearer and longer compliance, with potential flexibility through consultation and designated loading/unloading times. The project is set to launch in September 2018.

Lionel Messi scored the winning goal for Barcelona in their game against Atletico Madrid, extending his record as the competition's all-time top scorer, after missing training on Friday. This occurred on the same day that Real Madrid's Cristiano Ronaldo broke his club's record for league goals in a separate match.

Over 70 individuals, including players and directors from Italian third and fourth division clubs, are under investigation for "conspiracy to commit sporting fraud," with links to the 'Ndrangheta crime syndicate, and police are investigating suspicious results in dozens of matches.

Spiderlings of a hybrid species between the Dolomedes plantarius found in Sussex and Suffolk were released in suitable dykes at Castle Marshes to promote genetic variability, improve adaptation to environmental changes, and help the new population cope with climate change impacts, with support from Natural England, Suffolk Wildlife Trust, and the BBC Wildlife Fund.

In August 1947, India and Pakistan gained independence from British rule (Partition), resulting in mass displacement, as summed up in the special CBBC documentary "Finding My Family - Partition: A Newsround special," sharing one woman's account of the personal impact on her family.

Iva Barr, a veteran marathon runner with 30 years of experience, participated in her 20th marathon despite having to take a detour due to fatigue. Despite not completing the full route, she enjoyed the event, was moved by the support of the young people, and has no regrets about her final attempt.

China's top cities are experiencing skyrocketing property demand, with some extreme measures like fake divorces being employed, yet unaffordable for young workers with low wages despite the central bank's efforts to curb the rising prices.

A 46-year-old landlord named Mr Jones was found dead at The Blossoms public house in Holyhead, and a 24-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of murder. Police are appealing for witnesses from an Arriva Bus that passed the Black Bridge area during the incident.

The article invites readers to follow BBC News Entertainment on various social media platforms, including Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram, or send them story suggestions to entertainment.news@bbc.co.uk.

A red Ford Fiesta and a white Asda delivery van collided on the A713 near Carsphairn at around 10:40 on Friday, resulting in the deaths of both drivers, Antony Sztuka (50) and Scott Kennedy (46), both from Ayrshire. Police are seeking information from witnesses who may have seen a white flat-bed pickup truck in the area at the time of the crash. The road was re-opened around 18:45 hours.

Australian rower Sarah Tait, who won an Olympic silver medal in 2012, has been a strong role model to many due to her accomplishments, including an Olympic medal, despite being diagnosed with cervical cancer in 2013.

On the day of Afghan President Ashraf Ghani's inauguration and following the signing of a US-Afghan deal allowing US troops to stay in Afghanistan, the Taliban claimed responsibility for two suicide bombings, injuring military personnel and civilians in two separate locations in Kabul.

Daimler expects its full-year sales to significantly exceed 100bn euros, despite a slower growth in Mercedes sales in China (8% compared to 82% in the previous quarter), with the CEO, Dieter Zetsche, projecting continued, albeit slower growth in major emerging markets, and expressing confidence in the company's ability to maintain and grow sales, despite the cooling market in China.

The 10-year-old son of Denmark's Crown Prince Frederik was rescued from a rip current by lifeguard Nick Malcolm at Mermaid Beach, with the lifeguard receiving personal thanks from the Prince. According to fellow lifeguard Stuart Keay, the prince might not have survived without the timely rescue.

An elderly man was found deceased on Elgin Road at its junction with Inchbroom Road, with police and firefighters being called to the scene at 16:10 on Wednesday. Police are conducting a joint fire investigation, suspecting no foul play.

A specialized traumatic amputation clinic has opened at the Surrey-based Defense Medical Rehabilitation Centre (DMRC), catering to veterans with complex amputation-related complications. The program, managed by staff experienced in treating military casualties, will share knowledge and best practices with the NHS to provide the best possible care to veterans, acknowledging the significant sacrifices they made to protect Britain.

Enforcement cameras installed on a two-mile stretch of the M4 in Port Talbot have caught approximately 125 speeding drivers per day in less than a week, a decrease from the 700 daily violations during a pre-Christmas pilot period. The Welsh partnership aims to educate drivers about the dangers of excessive speed while viewing enforcement as a last resort after considering engineering solutions.

A Manchester-born man, living in Spain, is accused of secretly photographing his students, sending child pornography online, and possessing a large number of sexually explicit files involving minors. Police found these files at his home, and believe he previously lived in Seville, Spain. They are currently attempting to identify the victims depicted in the images.

Sturgeon fish named Steve, worth up to £1,000, swam out of a water center during a flood, escaped, and has been found in a deep puddle a mile away, with minor injuries but otherwise healthy. A similarly valued koi carp named Chadwick is still missing.

Comedian and actor Chris Rock, known for his TV and film work such as Dr Dolittle, Madagascar, and Top Five, has filed for divorce from his wife Malaak after 19 years of marriage, asking for privacy while focusing on family. They have two daughters together, Lola Simone and Zahra Savannah. In a past stand-up routine, Rock humorously emphasized the importance of both parties in a relationship staying focused on the partnership.

A collision occurred on the motorway between Tamnamore, causing the closure in both directions, resulting in lengthy traffic delays. Police advise motorists to exit at either junction 12 or 15 depending on their destination, and urge anyone with information regarding the preceding events to contact them.

The French government has not yet received a response from the Vatican for the nomination of senior diplomat Laurent Stefanini as the new French ambassador to the Holy See, and the prolonged silence is being interpreted as a rejection, given the Vatican's tradition of not commenting on declined nominations and Mr. Stefanini's previous service at the Holy See and France's progressive stance on LGBTQ+ rights.

The Nasdaq experienced its largest one-day decline since April 2019, dropping 2.4%, as semiconductor, biotech, and other tech stocks fell sharply; this occurred alongside a decline in U.S. durable goods orders, causing a drop in the Dow Jones (1.6%) and the S&P 500 (1.5%).

Vondrousova, the Czech 233rd-ranked player, advanced to the brink of the top 100 by defeating Kontaveit and Strycova, while Coric, the Croatian 20-year-old 79th-ranked player, snatched a five-set victory over Kohlschreiber (3rd seed) to win his first ATP title at the Grand Prix Hassan II.

Stoke City signs Cameroon international Eric Choupo-Moting, who has played in the Bundesliga and Champions League, and has represented Cameroon at the World Cup and won 48 caps, scoring 13 goals, becoming their fourth signing of the summer.

A 56-year-old man with cerebral palsy, Seamus McCollum, died at a private nursing home in Randalstown, Maine last September, but his death was not initially treated as a murder case. The police launched a murder investigation in April this year after the autopsy results were revealed, and a woman is currently being questioned in connection to his death.

Heavy rains have deluged main streets in India's Tamil Nadu state, disrupting normal life, flooding 80,000 homes in Sri Lanka and causing evacuations, damaging infrastructure, and prompting a $75m relief fund from the state government, with the Chief Minister stating extreme rainfall has compressed typical monsoon conditions into just a few days.

A McGill's bus service caught fire on the A760 Kilbirnie Road, near Largs, on Saturday, but the driver and passengers managed to exit unharmed, thanks to the driver's quick actions. The incident resulted in the temporary closure of the road and the removal of the burnt-out bus, with the passengers needing only a cup of tea afterwards.

Jake Ball, a 25-year-old cricket player, has an impressive start to the 2016 County Championship season, leading Notts' bowling attack with six wickets in each of their first two games, making him the top wicket-taker in Division One. His performances have been praised by Notts' director of cricket and coach, with his focus on progressing his career with the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB). Despite his efforts, Notts suffered an eight-wicket defeat against Lancashire in their second match.

The article details the unveiling of a memorial stone, made from Jersey granite, in Guillemont, France, in honor of 120 Jersey men, known as "the Jersey Pals," who were killed during the Battle of the Somme in World War I. A part of the stone will be returned to Jersey to become part of a monument in Royal Square.

John Boyega, the former Theatre Peckham company member who portrayed Finn in Star Wars: The Force Awakens, is currently filming Star Wars Episode Eight, and he expressed his honor to give back to the theater where he started. The theatre's founder believes Boyega will be a tremendous inspiration for the young members given his success.

In the ongoing European Tour event, Thailand's Aphibarnrat and Fitzpatrick are tied at the top after impressive birdie performances, with Donald, Westwood, and 16 other players close behind; Bradley Dredge withdrew due to illness.

In the County Championship match, Middlesex has a strong position for their first win of the season, with Michael Voges (128*) and Dawid Malan (147) producing a crucial 279-run third-wicket partnership, despite losing early openers, while Hampshire looks to salvage a draw, with poor weather forecasted for the third day.

A 52-year-old woman died and a 16-year-old boy is critically injured following an incident on Penilee Road on Friday, with police releasing and subsequently locating a 54-year-old man they wished to question, while the site is cordoned off for investigations.

John Lennon's childhood home at 9 Newcastle Road, Wavertree, was bought by an anonymous telephone bidder in a "bidding war," catalyzed by its historical significance and proximity to Penny Lane, for an estimated price between £150,000 and £250,000, generating interest from both national and international buyers.

A man, Aaron Joseph, has denied owning a dog that caused fatal injury to David Ellam while out of control in public, pleading guilty to possessing cannabis on the same date; trial set for 5 February, with Judge Peter Collier QC hoping for a sooner date.

A body thought to be that of Thomas Bebbington, a 22-year-old man from Shrewsbury, was discovered on private land near Leighton, approximately 10 miles from Shrewsbury city centre, following his disappearance near the Dana Steps on 10th November.

Tiny five-week-old otters are being cared for in a medical facility and are currently being fed every six days, with hopes that they will reach a stage where they can be moved to a larger, outdoor habitat with live food in the summer.

A 33-year-old mother of four, Joanne Thompson, was found dead at her home in Old Mill Court, Newtownards, with the police seeking witness accounts of a disturbance at a bonfire in Dakota Avenue on Monday and any unusual activity around her house on Tuesday night and Wednesday morning.

A record-breaking 2,270 black-tailed godwits, more than double the previous record, spent the spring on Tiree island in the Hebrides, with the majority found in a small field in Kilmoluaig. Notably, some of the birds were from France, Portugal, and Spain, and Tiree officer for RSPB Scotland is optimistic about their successful breeding season in Iceland.

Rangers coach, Durrant, who previously worked with the first team during Walter Smith's second spell and under Ally McCoist, will not be returning for pre-season training under new manager Mark Warburton, indicating potential changes to the coaching personnel at Ibrox.
A rare albino deer, estimated to occur once in every 100,000 births, has recently been spotted and is drawing much attention from visitors.

A 15-year-old student named Asad Khan from Bradford died three weeks after starting at Beckfoot Upper Heatson School and his family suspects he was bullied, with the traumatic incident leading to his death. The coroner is considering calling a boy who had conversations with Khan to provide testimony during the ongoing inquest.

A 17th-century painting, believed to depict the 1654 coronation ceremony, was found at Rokeby Park, Barnard Castle, where it has been since at least 1880. The painting, which has not been valued, is unique as it is the only known painted representation of the ceremony, and its origin and artist are unknown. Experts have studied the painting but do not know who painted it.

Macclesfield Town defeats Wrexham 3-0, with Danny Rowe, Mitch Hancox, and Danny Whittaker scoring for Macclesfield, while Wrexham's Jordan White misses a late penalty. The win moves Macclesfield up to seventh place in the table, with Wrexham remaining in 15th.

"Africa's Football Confederation (CAF) has secured a new sponsorship deal with French oil and gas company Total, starting from the 2017 Africa Cup of Nations finals in Gabon. The exact amount of the deal has not been disclosed yet."

Spain coach Julen Lopetegui recalled Diego Costa and Juan Mata after missing Euro 2016, while Iker Casillas was overlooked ahead of World Cup qualifiers against Belgium and Liechtenstein, with David de Gea, Sergio Ramos, David Silva, and others also called up.

A large, deliberate wildfire is currently spreading over a 5km area, across a border, causing concern due to the risk it poses to lives, properties, and the countryside, with local authorities appealing to the public to stop such reckless behavior.

Irish cricketer Boyd Rankin, who briefly played for England between 2013 and 2014, is returning to Ireland's team, having agreed to a comeback after discussions with Cricket Ireland. He is eligible to play again due to ICC regulations and is available for upcoming matches, including the InterContinental Cup match with Papua New Guinea and the ICC World Twenty20 in India. Rankin hopes to aid Ireland in achieving Test status, a prospect that attracted him to return to the team.

The Northern Ireland Rare Disease Partnership, comprising of the Patient Client Council and created for sufferers and carers of rare diseases, seeks to enhance treatment and care through education, provision of specialized services, and advocacy to ensure a voice for those impacted by rare diseases who have limited means of representation.

Gloucester Cathedral plans to establish a girl chorister program, aiming to discover talented young singers from diverse backgrounds, encouraging them to participate in the cathedral's musical worship, and ensuring their continued presence for future services.

Chelsea winger Pedro was taken to the hospital after suffering an injury during a game in Beijing, stayed overnight, and is expected to wear a protective mask when he returns to training, with the rest of the team now in Singapore for two upcoming matches.

Veteran cricketer James Taylor, who retired due to a heart condition in 2016, has returned to cricket coaching, working with Nottinghamshire and Yorkshire's academies as well as offering media commentary. James is noted for his impressive 50-over record, averaging over 50. Former Northants captain David Sales, with over 22,000 runs and 20 years at the County Ground, will work on technically enhancing the squad's batting skills.

A man is scheduled to appear in court on December 5 for on-road criminal damage, disorderly behavior, and assault on police, with the incident occurring at 15:00 GMT on Friday afternoon on Whiterock Road, and reportedly witnessed by people picking up prescriptions, including children.

A yacht's engine failed a mile north-east of Muck Island on Thursday evening, prompting a volunteer crew from the Larne RNLI to launch two lifeboats and tow the yacht to Carrick Marina, successfully completing a joint operation of their inshore and all-weather lifeboats.
Ipswich clinched a thrilling 4-3 victory over MK Dons with David McGoldrick scoring three times, while opposing manager Karl Robinson lamented a season of mixed performances.

A motorist from Darlington is facing charges for dangerous driving and causing serious injury, as well as counts of criminal damage, after a bridge fell onto the London-bound carriageway of a motorway on August 27, injuring a motorcyclist with broken ribs. The event took place between junctions four and three, near the M26 link, and closed the main route to the Channel Tunnel and Port of Dover, requiring two large cranes to clear the debris initially and requiring a re-closure the following weekend to remove the remaining bridge debris.

In the Spanish town of Platja d'Aro, a prank involving a fake celebrity chase resulted in injuries to 11 people and the hospitalization of 3, and selfie sticks were mistaken for weapons. The German newspaper Die Welt reports that several Germans were involved in the flashmob, which was organized on social media.

Two individuals, Sindyann Regis and Chevaze Mcgregor, are charged with the murder of a two-and-a-half-year-old boy named Jeremiah Regis, who was found with over 100 injuries, including a chest bite, at an address in Wolverhampton. The alleged crime took place on November 20, with the post-mortem examination revealing Jeremiah died of abdominal peritonitis caused by blunt force trauma. The case was adjourned until December with a provisional trial date set for 25 April. The family of the deceased boy described Jeremiah as a "lovely, quiet, innocent little boy who was always smiling."

A large gorse fire on Woodbury Common, Devon, is causing difficulties for firefighters due to high winds and a lack of water supplies, resulting in four cases of smoke inhalation and one hospitalization with burns. Fire crews are working to contain multiple fire fronts, with a police helicopter monitoring the scene. Evacuation of the nearby Woodbury Park Golf and Country Club is happening as a precaution. Smoke is visible for miles around.

The British Speedway Promoters' Association, led by chairman Keith Chapman, has reached an agreement to secure the club's future, and a 15-year lease has been signed for the team's Beaumont Park venue. Upcoming meetings are planned to finalize the management structure, race night for the 2017 season, and other arrangements.

Elizabeth Bowe, aged 50, died three days after being severely injured at Bobby Jones Place in St Andrews, and her brother Charles Gordon, aged 51, was charged with her murder, following an initial police response investigation ordered by the Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service (COPFS), with findings to be reported in due course by the Police Investigations and Review Commissioner (PIRC).

A former Celtic and Motherwell midfielder, Jim O'Brien, has returned to Ross County on a two-year permanent deal, bringing valuable experience to aid the development of younger players. He may be unavailable for the Scottish League Cup encounter with Hibernian until international clearance is obtained.

In Division Two, Northants take early control of the game against struggling Durham, reducing them to 126 all out with regular wickets and dismissing key batsmen like Paul Collingwood and Michael Richardson. Despite a poor start, Northants salvage the day with Max Holden and Chesney Hughes unbeaten on 19 and 16 respectively, leaving them 59-3, 107 runs behind.

Lydia Ko, a New Zealander, trails the joint leaders Brooke Henderson and Lee Mi-rim by one stroke after two rounds at the Sahalee Country Club women's major, with Henderson and Lee at two under, and Catriona Matthew at one over following a three-under round. Only five players, including Americans Gerina Piller and Brittany Lincicome, are under par at the halfway stage. Ko expresses gratitude for her putter in maintaining her position. Henderson is content despite losing the lead by one shot following a one-over round on a challenging day with fluctuating weather conditions.

Scotland manager Gordon Strachan has appointed former footballer Steve Watson as his assistant, reuniting the duo who played together at Aberdeen in the 1970s and 1980s. Watson steps into the role following the departure of Stuart McCall, who moved to manage Bradford City. Watson had previously worked with Strachan during the Euro 2008 qualifying campaign.

Giants take a commanding lead over Belfast with goals from Shields, Martinelli, Garside, Foster, and Saviano in a 5-1 victory. Meanwhile, Cardiff and Coventry are preparing for their match following the Devils' win over Coventry in the previous evening's game.

Jordan Spieth, the defending champion, suffered a sudden collapse on the final day of the Masters, with a quadruple-bogey seven on the 12th hole, allowing Danny Willett (the first Englishman since Faldo in 1996) to win the tournament.

The article provides instructions on how to submit photos for England's Big Picture, including email, Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram, with a preference for recent photos, and the requirement to agree to the BBC's Terms and Conditions and grant a royalty-free license for publication.

The trial is ongoing for Honey Rose, an eye specialist, who is accused of gross negligence manslaughter for allegedly failing to detect swollen optic discs during a routine eye test on Vincent Barker (Vinnie), leading to a build-up of fluid in his brain, which eventually resulted in his death.

Inflation in food prices increased by 4.9% in June, partially due to rising pork prices, while the overall inflation rate remains below the government's target. This development, along with concerns about a property bubble and global economic uncertainty, has led analysts and economists to predict that China will maintain its monetary policy in a neutral position, avoiding both interest rate cuts and tightening. Additionally, China expects economic growth in 2013 to be the slowest in 23 years at 7.5%. The actual GDP data for the second quarter of the year will be released on 15 July.

Ivorian footballer Cheick Tiote, aged 30, passed away after collapsing during training with Chinese second-tier club Beijing Enterprises on 5th June; former teammates and family paid tribute to him at his memorial, with Senegal striker Papiss Cisse stating Tiote was like a brother to him.

In the fifth stage of the race, Slovak cyclist Peter Sagan won an uphill sprint, propelling him to second overall behind leader Nairo Quintana. Geraint Thomas moved up to sixth overall for Team Sky, with two stages remaining.

Cuadrilla's fracking plans at Preston New Road, worth around £50 million, have been approved, despite a pending legal challenge by opponents. The firm plans to prioritize Lancashire for jobs, investment, and community initiatives, with approximately half of the funds expected to be spent locally. The site's building contract has been awarded to Bolton-based AE Yates Ltd and work is expected to start early next year, with an "independently audited tracker" monitoring Cuadrilla's pledges.

Three teenage boys from north-west London, missing in March amid concerns about plans to travel to Syria, were arrested in Turkey, detained at Istanbul's Sabiha Gokcen airport, but later released without charge. This event occurred several weeks after three schoolgirls from east London, believed to have traveled to Istanbul and possibly Syria, went missing.

Hospital respiratory consultant Dr Christopher Davies criticized the hospital management for purchasing an overpriced blackout blind, while the hospital maintains that they followed NHS requirements and firmly rejected the quote, with NHS England investigating the situation.

Swansea City's development squad, led by Adam King, secured the league title with a draw against Wolverhampton Wanderers in March, and won the cup final to amass 31 wins across all competitions in the 2016-17 season, while the senior team narrowly avoided relegation from the Premier League.

Following severe winter storms in December 2013 that caused damage to a dune system at Barkby Beach in Prestatyn, a report suggests the dunes are re-establishing themselves naturally. However, the council plans to create a secondary dune system to increase defense against potential breaches, as the narrowness of the existing dunes presents a serious concern. This decision comes after homes were evacuated and properties lost power during flooding in Rhyl, Denbighshire, one of the worst-hit areas.

The article announces that the FA Cup match between South Shields (Northern League Division One) and Bridlington Town (Northern Counties East League), taking place on 19 August at 12:30 BST, will be live-streamed across BBC Sport's digital platforms, including PC, mobile, and connected TV. Viewers can also watch the game live on BBC iPlayer, interact with the commentary team via #bbcfacup, and enjoy responses to messages as time allows. South Shields, captained by Argentine Julio Arca, previously won at Wembley in the FA Vase final.

In Edinburgh, a 38-year-old man suffered serious but non-life threatening facial injuries in a targeted attack on Craigmillar Castle Road on Friday night, while a 49-year-old victim did not require medical attention. Police are encouraging residents to report any suspicious behavior or vehicles seen in the area at the time to help establish the full circumstances of the incident.

A 51-year-old woman, Pamela McLaggan, pleaded guilty to manslaughter for the death of Jonathan Baines, also known as "Willy", following an event at Market Rasen races in Gainsborough, and was remanded in custody before being sentenced on 21 December.

A 15-year-old boy was attacked and sustains facial injuries, including an eye injury, by a man and woman in their 40s at Patterton station. The incident occurred around 23:30 on Saturday 3 October, and his mobile phone was stolen. The event took place during a busy service between Glasgow Central and Neilston, and British Transport Police are urging anyone with information about the attackers to contact them immediately.

A 17-year-old from Dewsbury was questioned by the North East Counter Terrorism Unit under the Terrorism Act in April, and two teenagers, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, are suspected of having traveled to Syria to join Islamic State in March, prompting an investigation by West Yorkshire Police and counter-terrorism officers. Hassan's brother, earlier convicted under the Terrorism Act at the age of 16, was found to have a guide to making napalm on his computer.

The Giants' forwards Boxill, Peacock, and Shields, along with netminder Stephen Murphy, are part of the 22-man squad for GB, aiming to progress to the final qualifying stage for the 2018 Winter Games in PyeongChang by beating Italy, Netherlands, and Serbia. Seventeen players from the previous silver-medal-winning team at the 2015 World Championship (Division 1B) are included in the squad. Additionally, host club Cortina will play against the Belfast Giants during the tournament in a series of matches held at the SSE Arena during the competition.

Matthew Perry is allegedly taping a contribution for a tribute to the show's creator James Burrows, not a full "Friends" reunion as expected, while his former co-stars are set to participate in the special airing on NBC on 21 February. Meanwhile, Perry is returning to the West End with his play The End of Longing, a dark comedy about four people approaching middle age, which runs from 2 February to 14 May.

Despite a storied career at various English clubs including Manchester United, Preston, Derby, Blackburn, Wolves, and Oldham, 31-year-old Jones is currently with Burnley, helping the team win the Championship title last season and starting their Premier League season with a defeat by Swansea.

Lawyer Joe Acquaro, a notable figure in Melbourne's Italian community, was slain, with investigators suggesting that underworld figures potentially targeted him due to a lingering tension in Melbourne's criminal underworld.

On July 15, 2017, Air France Flight 374 from Paris to Vancouver carrying 294 passengers, was diverted to Prestwick, Scotland due to a slight smell of burning on board. A second aircraft was sent to return passengers to Charles de Gaulle Airport.

A severe weather warning has been issued for coastal areas and north-western parts of Wales, especially Aberporth, Aberystwyth, and Anglesey, as Hurricane Gonzalo reaches Britain on Monday night, bringing strong winds (up to 70mph in exposed coastal regions) and heavy rain from Tuesday, potentially causing disruptions and increased risk of surface water affecting roads, with some sailings between Holyhead and Dublin cancelled due to adverse weather forecasts.

The article discusses concerns about hospital overcrowding and long wait times, particularly affecting children, as exemplified by the experiences of patients Lilly and Jake, who had to endure lengthy waits for medical attention in a children's hospital in Sheffield.

A 34-year-old man from Poole was charged with causing grievous bodily harm, a 57-year-old woman from Poole was arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm with intent and perverting the course of justice, and bailed until July, following the fatal head injury of Kenneth David Dickie, 64, at the Rockley Park site in Poole, who later passed away at Southampton General Hospital.

A 24-year-old former Manchester United forward, Macheda, has extended his loan spell with Nottingham Forest until the end of the season, with manager Russell Slade also announcing the signing of midfielder David Vaughan on a one-year contract. A deal for midfielder Andre Moritz fell through due to complications in obtaining his release from his current Thai club.

The article reports that the body of missing worker Christopher Huxtable, who was one of four workers missing following a building collapse in February, was found on Wednesday. Despite the discovery, two other workers, Ken Cresswell and John Shaw, are still missing. Swansea East MP Carolyn Harris expressed her sadness for the family and urged the public not to forget the families of the two missing workers.

Bosnia-Herzegovina international is progressing from a hernia injury towards full match fitness, while Jordan Cousins has a season-ending quadriceps injury and Kazenga LuaLua is recovering from an ankle issue but doubtful for QPR's match. Bristol City coach Lee Johnson aims to secure a win against QPR to ascend positions in the league standings.

Italian astronaut Luca Parmitano, who was selected by ESA in 2009 and traveled to the International Space Station in 2013, fondly recalled his spacewalk experience as "absolutely fantastic" and immensely enjoyable, with him completing two spacewalks, orbiting Earth 2,656 times, and traveling over 110 million km in total.

Sixteen-year-old Joe Arundel, a former England Knights player, expressed excitement and a bit of nervousness about joining Hull FC, a large club known for fostering a winning mentality and nurturing promising young talent, according to Hull's club director of rugby, Shaun McRae.

Approximately 600,000 Ulster Bank payments are being worked on to be updated by Saturday to avoid customer inconvenience, following a recent IT issue similar to a 2012 major bank-wide IT meltdown that affected RBS and its subsidiaries. Since the 2012 event, the banking group has made significant investments to improve its computer systems.

In the 2016 Women's Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, Tanzania beat Kenya 2-1 with Omari Mwanahamisi scoring twice, while Kenya could not find an equalizer. In the third-place play-off match, also played on the day, Ethiopia defeated Uganda 4-1.

McDonald's Japan faces potato shortage due to industrial action in America, resulting in rationed French fry portions at their over 3,100 outlets, while supermarkets also struggle with butter shortages.

The article announces that the upcoming Classic Horse Race on June 3rd will feature prominent horses like Permian (winner of Dante Stakes at York) and Khalidi, increasing the overall purse to £1.625m. The favorite is John Gosden-trained Cracksman, who beat Permian in the Derby Trial. A 1,000-1 outsider Diore Lia is also set to race, despite having limited experience, to support Great Ormond Street Children's Hospital at the owner's request.

Athletico Madrid footballer Antoine Griezmann, their top La Liga scorer, has a haematoma on his left foot, resulting in a missed friendly against Ivory Coast for France, after an X-ray ruled out a bone injury, as his team prepares to play league leaders Real Madrid at home on March 6th, trailing them by six points after 11 games.

A veteran rugby league prop player, Willie Mason, who spent a 15-year career with five clubs in the NRL and played international rugby, is joining the struggling Super League side, St. Helens, after a season at Manly. He previously won the Premiership with Canterbury in 2004.

A new survey reveals an 11% increase of dog feces on UK beaches, with a sharp rise of 71% in Scotland, significantly affecting water quality and posing health risks for swimmers; the Marine Conservation Society notes the rise in plastic bag usage for mess cleanup, but encourages proper disposal in designated bins.

The Supreme Court ruled that the 2013 government-introduced fees for employment tribunal claims were unlawful and indirectly discriminatory, and that they prevented access to justice, particularly for women, as they ranged from £390 to £1,200 for a hearing and more for discrimination cases. This was a major victory for the trade union Unison, according to Dave Prentis, general secretary of Unison.

Dagenham & Redbridge suffered a defeat against Wycombe Wanderers, losing a player to red cards in both teams, with Wycombe moving up to sixth place while Dagenham remain in relegation spots. Manager John Still is optimistic about the team's potential, citing their ability to play well despite the disadvantage of playing with ten men.

Bee-eaters, native to southern Europe, have successfully nested for a second consecutive summer in the Low Gelt Quarry, drawing over 1,000 visitors to the RSPB viewpoint, with the chicks expected to fledge in the next few weeks.

A man's kayak capsized on the River Wey in Guildford and prompted a multi-agency search operation, as the public is urged not to enter the water themselves and call 999, despite the river being a popular kayaking spot, with nearby clubs warning it is not safe due to a flood warning and the river's fast-flowing nature.

A stone was thrown by an elephant at Rabat Zoo in Morocco, resulting in a girl being struck and later dying at the hospital. The event was captured on video and the zoo stated the enclosure met international standards, with experts suggesting the elephant may have been acting out of frustration or boredom, rather than targeting the girl specifically.

MP for North West Durham, Ms Glass, has joined the shadow cabinet amidst a wave of Labour MP resignations over the leadership of Jeremy Corbyn, with her predecessor, Ms Powell, stating that Corbyn's position as party leader is "untenable" due to the party's ineffective opposition.

Chelsea leads the English Premier League with 59 points, 5 points separating them from 6th-placed Manchester United, and six teams, including the Red Devils, are considered strong title contenders. Chelsea faces a challenging match against Burnley at Turf Moor, with the Clarets having won their last seven home games. Conte emphasizes the importance of focus and concentration for any team striving for the title.

Police and community support officers have implemented a dispersal order in Llangefni, allowing them to force troublemakers to leave, protect residents from anti-social behavior, and ensure the safety of young people from harm caused by excessive alcohol consumption.

The Netherlands international, Marten de Roon, participated in 33 Premier League games for Middlesbrough in the 2016-2017 season, scoring five goals, and Middlesbrough have expressed interest in signing Chelsea's Lewis Baker, with the midfielder being one of their targets for the upcoming season.

The Roald Dahl Funny Prize, an award for humorous children's books established by Michael Rosen in 2008, will be relaunched in 2016 to mark the author's centenary celebrations, with a goal to increase its impact and secure a robust future for this unique and successful prize.

Frazier Glenn Miller Jr, a 74-year-old white supremacist, was sentenced to death for a 2014 shooting in Kansas that resulted in the death of three individuals and the wounding of three others. Despite admitting to the crimes and expressing his desire to target Jewish communities before his death, he remained unrepentant during his sentencing.

The city council plans to introduce a larger self-service bike scheme, similar to London's 'Boris bikes', in April 2017, with 500 bikes located at various easily accessible sites, including district centers, universities, and strategic locations near public transport facilities, and financed through sponsorship income without costing the taxpayer.

Despite missing the entire season so far and undergoing back surgery, Senegal international Sakho is now undergoing light rehabilitation training and requires several weeks more to build up fitness before being considered for Premier League selection.

The NI Residential Property Price Index shows a marginal 0.8% rise in average property prices in Q3 2020 compared to Q2, with the biggest annual increase in Antrim and Newtownabbey (7.3%) and smallest in Ards and North Down (2.1%); terraced houses experience the highest annual growth (7.1%) while apartments see the smallest (4%). The overall average standardized price is approximately £124,000, and 5,200 deals were completed in the quarter.
A recent incident in Dumfries and Galloway illustrates the challenges of transporting large wind turbine parts on rural roads, as a lorry and its cargo ended up in a ditch on the A713.

The Betsi Cadwaladr health board suggested downgrading services, including maternity care, at Glan Clwyd Hospital due to staffing shortages, but a legal challenge halted this plan. Residents are protesting against the potential closure of maternity services at Wrexham Maelor and Ysbyty Gwynedd hospitals, arguing it would force women to travel further for care. The health board emphasizes any changes would be temporary, focusing on safety measures, and has created a website for public feedback on various proposals, including retaining all services. Several public meetings will occur in September to address concerns and gather input from residents.

Du Preez scored 116 runs off 99 balls and Klaas took two early wickets as South Africa beat Ireland by 68 runs, taking a 1-0 lead in the ODI series, with the remaining matches to be played on Tuesday and Thursday.

British high jumper Katarina Peake, aged 30, seeks to break her own Welsh record and secure a Team GB spot for the Rio Olympics by achieving a personal best of 4.50m at the Cardiff International Sports Stadium and equaling the Rio qualification standard.
A fire, believed to be deliberate, broke out at a building site involving scrapped railway sleepers in Llanwern, and lasted over 10 hours, with local police launching an investigation.

A charitable event, including a Nepal-themed concert, was held in Edinburgh, Scotland, initiated by the Nepal Scotland Association and Mercy Corps, aimed at raising funds for those affected by the recent devastating earthquake in Nepal, many of whom were friends and loved ones of Association members.

Neil Lennon, Hibernian's coach, was automatically suspended from the touchline for a return Europa League match due to a single instance of remonstrating with officials during the match against Brondby, following a controversial decision that led to a loss on penalties. Hibs have since appealed the suspension imposed by UEFA.

A fire occurred 1,100m beneath the sea bed at the ICL UK Boulby mine, seven workers were hospitalized, and an improvement notice was served by the Health and Safety Executive. The company has pledged to cooperate with the investigation and take measures to enhance safety procedures.

A 23-year-old British man and a French tourist were caught naked and removed from the Unesco World Heritage site, Machu Picchu, for a minor morality offense; the Foreign Office is in contact with Peruvian authorities regarding the incident.

Ivan Rakitic, the 28-year-old Croatian international footballer currently playing for Barcelona, is set to sign a new contract on Friday, extending his deal with the club that includes a buyout clause of £109m.

A couple in Halstead suffered severe injuries after a two-hour ordeal of torture at their house on 26 April. The incident involved a break-in around 21:00 BST by three men, depicted in a CGI image as one black man and two white. Police are continuing to investigate the crime, with a detailed description of one suspect at 5ft 10in tall, following multiple leads. The woman remains critical, while the man is recovering from his injuries.

Dizzee Rascal is set to headline the opening night of the Wickerman Festival at East Kirkcarswell Farm near Dundrennan on 25 and 26 July, alongside Martha Reeves and The Vandellas, The Zombies, Big Country, and The Feeling. More acts, including the Saturday night headliner, will be announced in the coming weeks.

In the Aviva Premiership, Foden scored his third try in two matches as Saints beat Quins 24-3, with both players aiming to secure a spot in the England squad for the Six Nations tournament, as interim coach Stuart Lancaster prepares to announce his squad on Wednesday and hopes to recall Brown, who hasn't played for England since 2008. Brown, also 26, has been prolific for Quins, with 10 tries in 17 starts to help them lead the Premiership table, while Foden hopes Saints will provide several players for the England squad.

A fatal motorcycle collision occurred between a KTM motorcycle and a Vauxhall Zafira car in Dagenham, resulting in the 22-year-old motorcyclist's death. The 10-year-old rear passenger in the car suffered serious injuries, while the 7-year-old and 38-year-old driver were unharmed. No arrests have been made, and police are encouraging witnesses to come forward with information about the incident.

Pfizer, following the cancellation of its proposed $160bn merger with Allergan, has agreed a deal to acquire California-based Anacor Pharmaceuticals, whose flagship product, crisaborole, is a potential $2bn eczema cream awaiting FDA approval, as it aims to address a significant unmet medical need for eczema patients in the US, where an estimated 18 million to 25 million people currently lack safe and appropriate treatment options.

On Saturday at 23:00 BST, police responded to a street fight on Oxlow Lane, Dagenham, where they subsequently confiscated multiple weapons and cannabis and arrested two minors for possession of an offensive weapon and assaulting police, while reiterating no one was injured in the event. The incident concluded with the police praising their quick action and swift recovery of the weapons, suggesting they averted a potential tragedy.
A 23-year-old man from Cardiff was arrested on suspicion of sexual assault after an attack on a 19-year-old woman at Gorsedd Gardens near Cardiff Civic Centre.

Conservative MSP John Lamont resigned from the Ettrick, Roxburgh, and Berwickshire constituency to contest as a Westminster candidate, aiming to defeat SNP's Calum Kerr in the by-election for Scotland's most marginal Westminster constituency. The Liberal Democrats have nominated Catriona Bhatia as their candidate.

The EU Commission has approved the sale of beef from the UK, Ireland, France, and Germany to Canada, marking a significant shift following a Russian import ban and weaker Chinese demand, which has hit the EU's farm exports, particularly the dairy sector. This decision is due to Canada recognizing the EU's robust measures to eradicate BSE, a disease that led to significant losses in the 1990s. The US has also resumed importing beef from the EU, under strict monitoring.

The European Commission plans to impose sanctions on nations identified as tax havens if they fail to address concerns raised over their tax practices, following the Panama Papers leak, and has initiated negotiations for a unified EU list of non-cooperative jurisdictions, with discussions expected to be challenging and the final number of inclusions undetermined, while authorities also agreed on exchanging information about company owners and a potential crackdown on banks and tax advisers aiding offshore tax evasion.

Archaeologists discovered Bronze Age burnt mounds, pottery fragments, and remains of kilns used for drying grain at Torvean, which were believed to be used for heating water for cooking, washing wool, or small saunas, during construction of a road (West Link) in Inverness, Scotland.

Oldham Athletic won against Southend United, with Jonathan Forte and Main scoring the goals, while Oldham maintained a six-point gap above the League One relegation zone, with the match result not significantly affecting Southend's 13th-place standing.

Irish actor Lally, best known for roles in Glenroe, Ballykissangel, and various Irish language films, passed away peacefully after a short illness, leaving behind his wife Peggy and their children Saileog, Darach, and Maghnus.

The Derby City Council, needing to save £79m over three years, initially planned to close Moorways Pool to save £350,000 annually, but after receiving a 4,000-signature petition from campaigners and agreeing to repair the aging facility, they pledged to keep it open for a year, citing savings in back-office and management restructuring. The closure would have left only one other public pool in the city, potentially affecting teaching for 1,200 young swimmers each week.

Children previously held by Boko Haram are being temporarily detained by the Nigerian military after being released from Boko Haram-controlled areas, according to concerns raised by human rights groups, although the location and duration of the detention are not specified. The army has not made any comment on the issue.

In the last week, Hearts footballer Alexander suffered a broken cheekbone, and goalkeeper Gallacher twisted his ankle, leaving both in doubt for upcoming matches, and Neilson revealed he might consider signing experienced goalkeeper Lee Hollis as a replacement.

A professional basketball player, Chelsey Lee, played for Bucheon KEB Hana Bank in the Women's Korean Basketball League (WKBL) and won the rookie of the year award, but is under investigation for allegedly falsifying her and her father's birth certificates to claim South Korean heritage and violating league rules, leading to the suspension of her records, annulment of the team's records, and the removal of the extra quota for international players with Korean heritage, along with the resignation of the club's owner and head coach.

The article outlines the release of an app that samples wireless signals to see if data is flowing uninterrupted from routers to phones and tablets, according to Ofcom research that suggests wi-fi in six million homes and offices in the UK is not running as fast as it could be. The research also shows that 2.4 million UK homes, about 8%, cannot get speeds of 10Mbps or more, with rural areas and small businesses particularly affected.

Paul Pogba's emoji was displayed on boards at Old Trafford following his mixed performance against Liverpool, and he later acknowledged fans' support on social media. Zlatan Ibrahimovic, who scored the equalizer, praised Pogba for handling pressure and stated his personal aim is to help Manchester United win rather than individual awards. Ibrahimovic currently leads the Premier League Golden Boot race with 14 goals, tied with Diego Costa and Alexis Sanchez.

A man discovered a large metal object, resembling a car in size, in a remote river in Brazil, which was confirmed to be debris from Europe's largest telecommunications satellite, Alphasat, launched last year from the Kourou base in French Guiana. The Brazilian authorities will contact the UK Space Agency to collect the object, and residents have been advised to report any health symptoms, but the wreckage is not believed to be radioactive.

The article reports that James Purnell, a former BBC executive, warns that decriminalizing non-payment of the BBC TV license could cost the BBC £200m and lead to the closure of BBC Four, CBBC, and CBeebies due to increased non-payment. The decision on decriminalization will be discussed during BBC charter renewal talks in 2017, and Labour MP John McDonnell has called for BBCThree to be kept as a television channel in the renewal discussions.

Derry City lost their first game of the new Premier Division season to Finn Harps, with Ryan Curran and David Scully scoring for Harps, while Rory Patterson scored for Derry in injury time, but it was not enough for a comeback. The former Derry players Ryan Curran and Tony McNamee particularly impressed for Harps.

The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has announced that issuers of securities using distributed ledger or blockchain technology, such as Initial Coin Offerings (ICOs), must register offers and sales, aiming to protect investors and maintain market integrity. This comes after concerns about an investment bubble in the ICO market and the lack of protection for investors if an ICO-backed venture fails.

Operation Anagram, formed by Strathclyde Police in 2006 after Peter Tobin's murder and rape of Angelika Kluk in Glasgow, also led to his convictions for the murders of Dinah McNicol and Vicky Hamilton. Despite being scaled back, it will remain active and anyone with information can still contact the team via email. The operation has provided closure to the families of the victims, but efforts continue to determine if Tobin is responsible for other unsolved crimes due to the investigation's work piecing together his movements and relationships over decades. Tobin is currently serving three life sentences for these crimes.

In the Australian Grand Prix, Ferrari's Sebastian Vettel emerged victorious over Lewis Hamilton, who acknowledges Ferrari outperformed Mercedes but hopes to reverse the trend at the Chinese Grand Prix, with both drivers expressing optimism for an exciting season due to the close competition.

Southwark Crown Court heard that Mr Clifford, a former celebrity manager, is on trial for allegedly exposing himself and forcing a woman to perform a sex act, which he denies; his interview with police includes multiple "no comment" responses, and his trial has been adjourned until Monday, when he is due to give evidence.

Ospreys coach Steve Tandy expects an entertaining and physical match in France in the Pro12 tournament, with Nicky Smith set to return from injury and New Zealander scrum-half Brendon Leonard doubtful with a shoulder injury.

The annual Diwali celebration on Leicester's Golden Mile, known for its large firework display, attracted a significant number of people from various backgrounds, with a focus on unity and shared joy, and included additional events such as Rangoli street art, stage entertainment, and art and craft exhibits in other parts of the city.

Rosie's Helping Hands, a charity founded by parents Karen and John Ross in memory of their daughter Rosie Ross, who was murdered in 2001, has been active for 16 years and has raised £350,000 for young people in and around Aldridge. In summer 2017, the charity will wind down as the Rosses want to move past the painful anniversary of their loss, but they will continue to fundraise and support projects until then, including a pirate themed play area on the children's ward at Walsall Manor Hospital that has improved the hospital experience for pediatric patients.

Macmillan Cancer Support and Cwm Taf Health Board are planning to build a new £5 million palliative care unit at the Llantrisant site, which would provide inpatient, outpatient, and day care services for those with incurable cancer and other conditions, marking Macmillan's largest single investment in Wales; the center aims to improve access to specialist tests and treatment for patients, and the proposed design includes family-friendly amenities like a kitchen and common areas.

The article ranks North Wales as the fourth-best destination globally for travelers in 2021, with Surf Snowdonia and Zipworld at Pen rhyn in Llandudno, along with a cultural tour of northeast Wales, included in the list. Other new attractions added to the region include Choquequirao in Peru, Taranaki Airport in New Zealand, the Azores in Portugal, and more.

The Church of England and the Church of Scotland have committed to growing together in communion and strengthening their partnership in mission, as outlined in the Columba Declaration, which sets out shared foundations of faith and allows clergy and lay people to be welcomed into the other church when they move across the border, recognizing each church's constitutional responsibilities in separate parts of the UK.

L/Bdr Parkinson, a severely injured bombing survivor who carried the Olympic torch in the UK, garnered extensive support through Facebook but could not accept the abundant friend requests due to the site's limit of 5,000 friends per user.

A significant drug smuggling operation was intercepted at Beirut airport, with two tonnes of Captagon pills discovered in cases due to be loaded onto a private jet, reportedly involving Saudi citizens. This operation, which is the largest yet discovered at the airport, has added to its reputation as a major hub for Captagon trafficking.

The Sexual Offences, Exploitation and Child Abuse Command is conducting an investigation and Kids Company, a charity run by Camila Batmanghelidjh, is cooperating, prioritizing the safety of its clients while maintaining they have robust policies to protect them. The police and NSPCC are asking for any relevant information from the public.

The Queen, who turns 90 this week, is famous for her ability to mimic local brogues, especially at Sandringham in Norfolk, and her impressive Scottish accent from years spent at Balmoral in Aberdeenshire. She is known for her sense of humor, as demonstrated by her amusing stories, including encounters with shoppers who don't recognize her. The Queen will celebrate her birthday at Windsor Castle, where gun salutes will be held and beacons will be lit at the highest points of the four countries of the UK.

The United Nations Agency for Human Settlements' report indicates that Latin America, the world's most urbanized region, experiences extremely high income inequality, with the richest 20% earning 20 times more than the poorest 20%. The region, which is at the end of an era of urban expansion, has shown reductions in poverty, indigency, and unemployment, and is positioned to transition towards a focus on quality of life, equity, and sustainability, particularly addressing the cited challenges of job deficit and labor informality.

A Carmarthenshire Labour councillor, Tegwen Devichand, is under investigation for sharing a Facebook post that supported the death penalty for sex offenders, which was initially posted by the far-right group Britain First. She also opposes plans to remove English-stream education at Ysgol Llangennech, sparking controversy within her party. Plaid Cymru accuses Labour members of collaborating with UKIP to undermine the council's decision and has called for the party to investigate and address the issue.

The Iraq War Families Campaign Group, led by relatives of British soldiers killed in the Iraq War, launched a crowdfunding campaign to determine the feasibility of potential legal action against individuals involved in the conflict, following the publication of the Chilcot report. The report criticized former PM Tony Blair for overstating the threat posed by Saddam Hussein and sending troops into battle unprepared, but did not make a definitive finding about the legality of the UK's military action in Iraq. The funds raised will be used to pay for legal counsel to provide an opinion on the feasibility of pursuing legal action against key individuals involved in the invasion of Iraq.

Syed's defense team is given the opportunity to reopen the case for the 1999 murder of Hae Min Lee, as a judge in Baltimore allows for the submission of new evidence, including questions about the accuracy of mobile phone records used in the original trial and the testimony of a potential alibi witness who claims to have seen Syed in a library at the time of the crime, a fact overlooked by his original legal team.

A 16-year-old boy who attended a party in Dundee last November, pulled a machete on a taxi driver upon their return to the party, prompting one of his friends to steal the driver's change. The attacker had previously served custodial sentences for assaults committed when he was 14 and 15. The boys will be sentenced next month after social work background reports have been prepared.

John Clancy, Labour councillor for Quinton, has been elected as leader of Birmingham City Council following five bids in the ballot by the authority's 78 Labour councillors, succeeding Sir Albert Bore. John Clancy has pledged to focus on providing new homes, expanding regeneration outside the city center, and offering free school meals for primary school children. He will take office on December 1st and will face challenges to make rapid improvements in order to avoid continued scrutiny from government commissioners. The council is currently under scrutiny from a government-appointed review panel, following commissioner Sir Bob Kerslake's recommendation, following reports of corruption and mismanagement associated with the so-called Trojan Horse letter.

The interview for June's Empire magazine featuring actor Moore discussed his early meetings with Bond director Guy Hamilton, where they aimed to avoid deliberate comparisons to Sean Connery, while the series also included producer Barbara Broccoli reflecting on how Connery revolutionized the traditional image of a leading man in the franchise, and the role of "unsung hero" Yat Malmgren and Dr No scriptwriter Terence Young in shaping Connery's portrayal of Bond.

Witches' marks, believed to offer protection during the era of widespread belief in witchcraft and the supernatural, are symbols found in various medieval buildings in the UK, mostly from 1550 to 1750. These symbols, which can take various forms including the "Daisy Wheel" and letters, are being studied by Historic England this Halloween to document their occurrence in houses, churches, and other buildings, shedding light on past religious and superstitious beliefs.

During a session of Prime Minister's Questions, Jeremy Corbyn compared Prime Minister Theresa May's approach to Brexit negotiations to the character Baldrick from the comedy show Blackadder, saying her strategy was to "have no plan." May responded by noting that the actor who played Baldrick, Sir Tony Robinson, was a Labour member.

The Liverpool County Court ruling, in a case involving Jet2 and passenger Kim Allen, has rejected airlines' arguments to delay compensation payments for flight delays exceeding three hours, stating that justice delayed is justice denied. The court's decision is expected to encourage thousands of similar claims in the UK.

Jamie Dimon of JP Morgan warns that the number of jobs moving from the UK to the EU post-Brexit is dependent on EU regulations, while French reforms include incentives like lower taxes and English law courts for financial institutions considering a move.

China denies reports of deploying surface-to-air missiles on Woody Island in the Paracels, claiming self-defense facilities are legal under international law, while the US and other nations are concerned about China's military development in the South China Sea, an important shipping route that is also disputed territory among multiple claimant states, including Vietnam and Taiwan, and may become a flashpoint with global consequences.

Spider silk draglines enable Adanson's house spiders to stabilize and control their landing, giving them a significant advantage in capturing prey. Scientists suggest this mechanism could inspire the design of miniature, maneuverable robots.

The Supreme Court ruled that the UK government is not legally bound to consult with devolved legislatures, including Wales, when triggering Article 50 of the EU treaty, but there is a possibility that the Welsh Assembly may have a vote on the issue, influencing but not vetoing the process.

The Co-op Bank is nearing a rescue plan with existing investors to alleviate regulatory concerns, while ongoing negotiations aim to separate its pension fund from the Co-operative Group's scheme, in hopes of appealing to potential buyers drawn to the bank's ethical stance and four million customers.

Tidal Lagoon Power and Natural Resources Wales have competing estimates about the potential impact of the Swansea tidal lagoon project on fish populations, with NRW estimating a 21% salmon and 25% sea trout death rate annually, while TLP estimates a worst-case scenario of the lagoon killing 2% of all fish species. The project's viability is being considered by the UK government, with the Welsh Government seeking clarity on the UK government's position.

The article summarizes the chaotic, sexist, and hilarious moments from the latest season of the British reality show "The Apprentice," highlighting instances of outdated gender stereotypes, confusing presentations, lost team tours, and unsuccessful tasks, all leading to candidates' eventual dismissal, providing viewers with a sense of schadenfreude.

The Home Affairs select committee found that the cap on visas issued to skilled workers from outside the EU, particularly nurses with job offers in the UK, has resulted in a large number of rejections and could have led to a crisis in the NHS this winter. However, the committee's conclusion that the cap has had no effect on reducing net migration is disputed, as net migration rose by 30% in the year to June, to 336,000 - more than three times the intended target.

An off-duty British soldier named Matthew Boyd was fatally attacked outside a bar called The Cellar in Brecon, Wales, after which his attacker, Jake Vallely, was found guilty of murder but his friend Aaeron Evans was cleared of manslaughter charges. The trial heard that Vallely had been on a prolonged drinking binge before the attack, during which he boasted about being the "hardest man in Brecon." The unconscious body of Boyd, a member of the Royal Gibraltar Regiment, was found by police in the early hours of 8 May. The incident was described as a "despicable act" that "shocked" the community of Brecon, and a family tribute described Boyd as an "all-rounder" with a "promising career ahead of him" that was cut short.

The BBC, in partnership with This Place, has developed a brainwave-reading headset that allows users to select and operate BBC's iPlayer on-demand platform by concentrating or relaxing their minds, with potential future applications for helping those with disabilities.

The Chief Inspector of schools in Wales, Meilyr Rowlands, stated that the focus on certain performance measures discourages schools from providing adequate support to more able students, potentially stifling their progress. The Welsh Government has recognized the need to support these students more effectively, planning changes to the system used to measure schools' performance and introducing initiatives like the Seren Network to help more able students reach top universities.

The forthcoming album, Out Among the Stars, features previously unheard recordings by Johnny Cash, recorded in 1981 and 1984, and includes duets with June Carter and Waylon Jennings. These recordings were found in a vault in 2012, marking the fourth posthumous release since Cash's death in 2003. John Carter Cash, according to the BBC, believes these unreleased recordings are a work of art and are worth releasing as they would add to Cash's existing legacy of selling over 90 million records and championing the underdog.

The tribunal ruled that Maria McKeith was unfairly dismissed by the Ardoyne Association due to her role as a primary carer for her disabled daughter, a violation of the Disability Discrimination Act 1995. The Court of Appeal upheld the decision, awarding her compensation for injury to feelings, loss of earnings, and interest. Employers were reminded of their responsibilities under the law to protect against discrimination towards disabled individuals and their primary caregivers.

Scottish midfielder Kenny McLean Dorrans, who spent seven seasons at West Bromwich Albion and had two loan spells at Norwich City, has joined Rangers, marking his long-awaited return to Scotland after signing a three-year deal.

Scottish teams Team Brewster and Team Muirhead, led by Glen Muirhead (brother of winning skip Eve), defeated David Murdoch's Olympic silver medallists and Hannah Fleming's team respectively, to secure the men's and women's berths for the European Championships in Scotland starting from 19-26 November. Both teams, including returning player Anna Sloan, are looking forward to playing in a home event, with Eve Muirhead expressing excitement about representing her country in Scotland and Glen Muirhead highlighting the motivational advantage of playing on home soil.

The article discusses a disagreement between Councillor Pierre Oxley and Peter Halliday over transparency regarding details of a planned beach defense project, with Oxley questioning the composition of materials to be used and Halliday asserting transparency throughout the process, while the council prepares to address the concerns in an upcoming meeting.

John Nelms, co-owner of Dundee Football Club, announced a land use application will soon be submitted for land in Camperdown Park, aiming to improve the club's facilities, as they grapple with a £530,000 operating loss and challenges in maintaining their 19th-century stadium.
Chris Froome finished 8 seconds behind Spain's Jesus Herrada in the second stage of the Criterium du Dauphine, with overall leader Alberto Contador 13 seconds ahead.

The bodies of ex-EastEnders star Sian Blake, 43, and her sons, Zachary, 8, and Amon, 4, were found at the family home in London on Tuesday. The police have classified the case as a triple murder inquiry and are seeking the children's father, Arthur Simpson-Kent, as a suspect, who is believed to have left the UK and traveled to Ghana. Concerns about Sian's welfare were passed to the Met Police, which launched a missing persons inquiry, and the IPCC will conduct a thorough investigation into the police's handling of the case.

Wimbledon tournament organizers announced that play will be held on the traditional rest day (Middle Sunday), for the fourth time in history, due to several matches being halted over five days, in order to maintain parity in the tournament schedule and avoid excessive congestion in the women's draw.

Dutch manager Dick Advocaat, who saved Sunderland from relegation in the 2014-2015 season, unexpectedly decided to leave the club after eight games at the end of that season, citing a promise to his wife. He had initially agreed to stay until the end of the season. The assistant coach, Zeljko Petrovic, also left the club. Sunderland are the only team below Newcastle in the Premier League table, with a record of just one win that season, against League Two side Exeter City in the League Cup.

Russia's economy is projected to experience a 0.8% decline in GDP next year, following a 0.6% growth in 2014, due to the impact of reduced energy exports, oil price slump, and Western sanctions, which have resulted in a 6% drop of the rouble against the dollar this year, contraction in various economic sectors (except energy, mining, and retail trade), increased bank deposit guarantee, and direct recapitalization of major banks to avoid another financial crisis similar to 1998.

Presidential candidate Raila Odinga has accused Kenya's electoral authorities of fraud and is taking the dispute to the Supreme Court, claiming evidence of massive irregularities in the recent election, while international observers continue to deem the election free and fair and urge calm amid fears of potential violence.

A 60-year-old scuba diver suffered a cardiac incident while diving at Agincourt Reef, resulting in his death after CPR efforts were unsuccessful. It was the third incident in two days involving tourists at the reef.

The UK, Scottish governments, and Dundee City Council have agreed a 3.7 million pound contract with Loganair to continue operate the Dundee-London Stansted route for two more years, with funding divided among the three entities. The service will operate two weekday return flights and one Sunday flight. The route aims to maintain connectivity, support trade, tourism, and attract further routes.

The World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) begins offering its video streaming service in China through its partner PPTV, aiming to find local stars and tap into a potentially lucrative market. Chinese sports stars like Li Na (tennis) and Yao Ming (basketball) have shown the importance of having stars in the market, but competition for the same demographic is fierce.

Three men, including a West Midlands police officer, are being questioned for conspiracy to pervert the course of justice, as they allegedly provided false and malicious information suggesting a terrorist plot to kidnap an officer, causing a heightened alert and misconduct allegations.

Ireland secured a 4-1 victory over Poland in a must-win match of the World League 3 quarter-finals, with goals by McKee (twice), Eugene Magee, and O'Donoghue. Craig Fulton, Ireland coach, highlighted strong team play and the team's success in capturing the ball in critical areas, even though they left several more scoring opportunities. The winners, Ireland, will advance to the semi-finals on Saturday, facing Wales. France and Scotland will compete in the other semi-final at the same venue.

Philip Craig, a 38-year-old man from Leeds, was sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum of 25 years for the murder of 24-year-old Christopher Laskaris, who was living with Asperger's Syndrome and bi-polar disorder, in Leeds in November. Craig had pleaded guilty to burglary in a previous hearing and was also serving a three-year sentence for the crime at the time of the murder. Craig returned to the flat after the murder to steal items but the victim's body was not discovered until 17 November, 13 days after the murder. The charges against a second man, Dempsey Pattison, who was also charged with the murder, were dropped in February.

The Metropolitan Police has closed its reinvestigation into the 2010 death of Kester David, a man believed to have been killed for working as a police informant, acknowledging previous failings in their initial investigation, including not checking CCTV or interviewing witnesses promptly. Despite several appeals, no arrests have been made in connection with his death.

In 2015, football had the highest total attendance with 43.4 million, followed by three horse racing events in the top 10. Rugby union improved with the Rugby World Cup, reaching 7.5 million. Notably, Wimbledon was the most attended individual event with just under half a million spectators. British Grand Prix in Formula 1 had the highest attendees-per-event-day. Two new events, MotoGP's British Grand Prix and Badminton Horse Trials, replaced the Ryder Cup and Aintree Grand National in the top 10. Overall attendances increased by 6% compared to the previous year, although the total was lower than the record set in 2012 due to the Olympic and Paralympic Games in London and the Rugby World Cup in 2015.
