Future major UK sports events include the UCI Track Cycling World Championships, the European Aquatics Championships, and the FIH Women's Champions Trophy in hockey.

Beyoncé topped the Forbes list of highest-earning musicians in 2013-2014 with an estimated $105 million, followed by Taylor Swift at $64 million, Pink at $52 million, Rihanna at $48 million, and Katy Perry at $40 million. The calculations were based on income from touring, record sales, publishing, merchandise sales, endorsements, and other ventures. Madonna, Nicki Minaj, and Alicia Keys were also mentioned as high-profile artists who missed out on a spot in the top 10. The estimates were obtained by looking at data from Nielsen SoundScan, as well as interviews with managers, lawyers, and executives. The full list includes the earnings of additional artists such as Jennifer Lopez, One Direction, and Justin Timberlake.

The Scottish National Party claims it has a larger number of MPs than Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn, but Speaker John Bercow recognizes Labour as the official opposition due to the larger number of MPs it currently has, although Corbyn lost a formal vote of no confidence and several members of his shadow cabinet resigned.

The villagers of Crickhowell have successfully launched a bid to buy The Corn Exchange and convert it into independent shops with flats above, under the management of a new company called Corn Exchange Crickhowell Ltd, after a deal was reached with Punch Taverns, subject to contract.

RIT Capital will not make a formal bid for Alliance Trust, which is engaged in a strategic review that could lead to a sale, and has taken the company out of the UK's formal takeover and merger procedures.

Alexis Scott, 39, a former Police Community Support Officer, was convicted for tricking long-haul airline passengers into thinking they had excess cash on them during flights in April 2013. She was sentenced to time in prison, splitting her from her young daughter, due to the severity of the predatory crime that exploited victims' panic and affected international trust in the UK.

Educational platform TrueTube has received three award nominations for its drama and learning categories, notably for the films Refugee and Katie. Horrible Histories, meanwhile, earned three nominations for its special Shakespeare episode, with the Bafta Children's Awards recognizing various other films, animations, games, and programs across multiple categories, including Star Wars: The Force Awakens and Zootropolis. The awards ceremony will take place at the Roundhouse in London on 20 November.

Lady Mary Soames, the last survivor of Sir Winston Churchill's five children, bequeathed a collection of Churchill's artworks, including "Coast Scene near Cannes" and "View From a Bathing Hut at the Miami Surf Club," to the National Trust, Houses of Parliament, and Churchill War Rooms. These works were accepted in lieu of inheritance tax to commemorate the 50th anniversary of Churchill's death. Additionally, a painting by Sir John Lavery of Churchill at his easel and the Aly Khan Gold Cup, won by Churchill's horse, High Hat, were also part of the collection. Lord Vaizey stated that these paintings allow the public to appreciate Churchill's artistic talent as well as his political greatness.

An ex-investigator from the ombudsman's office was arrested for alleged theft of sensitive security documents containing information potentially endangering lives. This has raised concerns among the police federation, officials, and a local politician about the ombudsman's office's handling of sensitive material and the need for independence in investigations. The police have begun a criminal investigation and temporarily halted the release of further sensitive materials to the ombudsman's office while they review security protocols.

Phyllis Schlafly, a conservative advocate and outspoken opponent of feminism, abortion, and the Equal Rights Amendment, was an influential figure in the 1970s and helped create a political environment that aided in Ronald Reagan's presidency. She is remembered as an iconic American leader by her conservative group, the Eagle Forum, and was credited by Donald Trump as a patriot and champion for women.

Twenty-three-year-old rugby player Morgan is leaving Bristol at the end of the season to continue his career development in a Welsh team, primarily playing as full-back but also covering fly-half positions, in search of national Welsh team consideration.

The article details the trial of two people smugglers, Mufawaka Alabash and Asem Alfrhad, charged with the death of Syrian toddler Alan Kurdi, who became a symbol of the refugee crisis. Despite being found guilty of people smuggling, they were acquitted of causing death through deliberate negligence. Alan's family, including his brother Galib and mother Rihan, also lost their lives attempting the same crossing. The discussion revolves around the ongoing migration crisis and potential solutions, such as talks between European Council President Donald Tusk and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, which include the idea of "shipping back" migrants arriving in Greece from Turkey.

Former Milan station chief Robert Lady, convicted in absentia for his involvement in the 2003 abduction of Egyptian cleric Abu Omar who was allegedly tortured, was arrested and is reported to have fled to the United States after his trial in Milan, which was the first involving the CIA's practice of transferring suspects to countries where torture is permitted, according to Italian media reports.

Passenger numbers increased at Edinburgh and Glasgow airports for January 2017, with growth in international traffic, particularly on routes to Toronto and Dubai. Meanwhile, Aberdeen International Airport saw a decline in passenger numbers, with decreases in helicopter traffic due to weather conditions and maintenance issues. Ryanair plans to add new links to Faro and the Faroe Islands from Aberdeen in May.

The most-watched video on YouTube, Gangnam Style by Psy, has surpassed the previous view limit of 2.147 billion views, prompting YouTube to update its counter system to a 64-bit integer with a new maximum view limit of 9.22 quintillion views.

England aim to put their best performance together in the upcoming match against Sri Lanka to secure a semi-final spot in the World Twenty20. Despite a rocky start with losses to West Indies (opening match) and close calls against Afghanistan (57-6), England are looking to build on their win against South Africa. The struggling middle-order of defending champions Sri Lanka, who lost their opener to the West Indies but recovered against Afghanistan, presents an opportunity for England. Alex Hales, who missed the Afghanistan game due to injury, may return to play against Sri Lanka. The article does not explicitly state that Sri Lanka is not as fearsome as they were in the past.

Inrix Roadway Analytics reports that Edinburgh and Glasgow rank as Britain's second and third most congested cities, with Edinburgh's traffic jams predicted to cost £2.8bn over the next decade and Glasgow's cost £2.3bn. London leads Europe with the most traffic congestion "pinch points," potentially costing the UK nationwide £61.8bn in wasted time by 2025.

In the 44th minute of a friendly, a deflected shot by Norway's Nordtveit off Sammy Clingan's heel beat keeper Lee Camp to give Norway a late first-half lead. Northern Ireland struggled to find a response, and Elyounoussi, Ruud, and another substitute extended Norway's lead over the remaining minutes. Northern Ireland's impressive start yielded few results, as they won just one of their last 14 friendlies.

Brussels remains on the highest alert level, with Belgian authorities investigating potential Paris-style attacks and issuing arrest warrants for Salah Abdeslam, who is suspected of involvement in the Paris attacks. French authorities are leading an international manhunt for Abdeslam, and two individuals (Ali O and Lazez A, both from the Brussels district of Molenbeek) have been taken into custody in Brussels.

There were multiple fatal explosions in Zaventem Airport and Maalbeek metro station in Brussels on March 22, causing numerous casualties, prompting national mourning, and increasing global security measures with potential links to previous attacks in Paris in 2015.

Sheffield City Council's Green Party councillor, Alison Teal, faces potential legal action for her involvement in protests against the city's tree felling program; the council asserts that the removal of street trees is lawful and necessary, having faced months of disruption by a handful of protesters, who were warned that their actions were unlawful. The letter was sent to the protesters several weeks ago, and works are still being disrupted, causing city-wide delays.

In New Zealand, about 416 whales have stranded themselves at Farewell Spit, South Island, resulting in almost 300 fatalities, making it one of the worst such incidents in the country, with the highest stranding rates in the world. Locals and conservation department staff are working together to refloat the survivors, as experts investigate various factors causing whale strandings, such as age, sickness, injury, navigational errors, and distress signals that attract other pod members. The incident highlights that many such incidents occur at Farewell Spit, where its shallow waters seem to confuse whales and hinder their ability to navigate, and was the same location of another similar incident in 2015, where at least half of at least 200 whales died.

Experienced prop forward Brian Mujati, with a history of playing at high levels in Super Rugby, Top 14, and Premiership, has been signed by Ospreys to provide injury cover for their current tight heads, Dmitri Arhip and Ma'afu Fia, particularly as the season progresses and the Challenge Cup quarter-final in April approaches. Coach Steve Tandy believes Mujati will add valuable experience to the squad and address the critical position of only having two fit tight heads in the team, given Rhodri Jones' potential involvement in the Six Nations squad.

The Gwynedd council has decided to proceed with establishing a new Church in Wales campus at Ysgol y Berwyn in Bala, with the merging of two local schools and the involvement of multiple religious and non-religious individuals in the shadow governing body, despite the Church in Wales denying allegations that they no longer support the project. The details of the proposal will be discussed at a future council meeting, and if all goes well, the campus is planned to open in September 2018.

The county council wants to save £100m over five years by having one organization run all services, but district councils prefer three councils, leading to disagreement over devolution plans. District councils argue for an elected mayor to secure more funding from the government, while the county council wants to avoid further cuts to local services. Residents are being consulted on the proposal ahead of a county council decision.

Edinburgh Rugby, led by Dickinson, aims to win the remaining five matches in a tough run-in to have a shot at playoffs or the top six, starting with a challenging away game against Newport Gwent Dragons and continue with Zebre, Leinster, Munster, and Cardiff Blues. Edward aims to eliminate errors and finish opportunities to improve their performances, following recent losses in five out of six games under their coach, Solomons.

The Northern Ireland Bat Group, led by Karen Healy, is caring for an unprecedented number of grounded, malnourished, and injured young bats. Volunteers are hand-raising and nursing these bats back to health before releasing them back into the wild, with a pre-release assessment including checking their flying ability and weight. She emphasizes the significant benefits bats provide as they eat large numbers of pests, and debunks common misconceptions that they drink blood and are blind.

The Supreme Court, in its second week of oral arguments since the death of Justice Antonin Scalia, is considering placing new limits on the federal law banning people convicted of domestic violence from owning guns. During these hearings, Justice Thomas broke his long silence at the court, questioning a lawyer about whether any law violation suspends a person's constitutional rights.

British travel company Responsible Travel, after watching a BBC programme, decides to remove half a dozen trips involving zoos from their offerings of 3,500 tours. The firm's boss, Justin Francis, argues most animals in zoos are not endangered and few examples exist of endangered species being successfully reintroduced after captivity. This decision received support from the Born Free Foundation, with president Will Travers praising the move towards reducing animal exploitation in zoos worldwide.

A child of primary school age has been found deceased at a home in Faringdon, leading to a 40-year-old woman's arrest on suspicion of murder. The community has been advised to seek reassurance from local police. Police tape and increased police presence remain at the scene, and anyone with relevant information is asked to call the police.

A British suspect, known as BM, is accused of two counts of breaching Section 23 of a TPIm order by failing to contact a monitoring company and report to a police station twice in January. The Home Office declined to comment on the case, while the opposition party has argued that TPIm may be less effective in combating terrorism than previous measures such as control orders. The defendant was granted bail pending a plea and case management hearing in July, with the trial date yet to be set.

Qualcomm, the world's largest supplier of smartphone chips, agreed to China's largest corporate fine, lowering its royalty rates on patents used in China's mobile phone market. This move is expected to benefit Chinese smartphone makers Xiaomi and Huawei. Qualcomm sees a positive outlook for its business in China, generating about half of its global revenue from the country.

Michelle Mellotte, 61, has been barred from practicing as a doctor in the UK, following a police investigation and medical tribunal, for fraudulently obtaining £10,000 from an Alzheimer's patient in 2010, using her professional role, and putting patients at risk, bringing disrepute to the profession, and breaching fundamental tenets of her role.

A man, aged between 30 and 49, and nearly 6 feet tall, was found deceased near the M54 motorway in Shropshire, England, wearing specific clothing from 2007-2008. Investigators believe he may have been a victim of a crime, with no matches found in missing persons DNA profiles. The remains are believed to have been undiscovered for up to three years.

The surprise discovery in Avebury, a 30m wide site known for its colossal stone circle, includes a "stone square circle" that is thought to be one of the site's earliest structures, potentially commemorating the first people's ancestral house, and offering insights into why the monumental complex was built.

Reading Borough Council's proposed parking scheme intends to relieve parking pressures at a hospital but faces opposition from hospital staff, residents, and a local resident who argue that it will exacerbate parking issues, particularly affect hospital staff and patients, and potentially make living in the area difficult. The council asserts it has previously consulted with the public on the principle of prioritizing parking for residents in the area and is seeking further public input.

U.S. Navy Petty Officer Aimee Mejia, 21, was involved in a three-car accident on Okinawa Island, injuring two people and driving under the influence with alcohol levels six times the legal limit. This is the latest incident involving U.S. troops based in Okinawa, eliciting renewed anger over their military presence. In response, the U.S. Navy has imposed stricter drinking restrictions on personnel amid ongoing investigations and increased training.

In a record-breaking tri-series, the Lions (England Lions), coached by former England captain, Andy Flower, displayed exceptional batting form, with several young players scoring over 150 runs. Notably, Sam Billings, Dawid Malan, and Harry Duckett, who amassed a 367-run partnership in a 425-1 total, stood out with their remarkable scores. Flower highlighted these performances, particularly Duckett's, as evidence of England's promising future in cricket.

Colombia and FARC rebels have agreed to continue peace talks in Havana following the release of three hostages, with a focus on de-escalating the conflict and addressing victim-family concerns. The negotiations, which began in 2012, aim to end five decades of conflict that has claimed around 220,000 lives. The next round of talks is slated for 10-17 December, with a possible resumption around mid-January.

The Save Oxfordshire Children's Centres Campaign, led by Jill Huish, held a "baby blockade" protest against Oxfordshire County Council's proposal to close 44 out of 48 children's centers and replace them with eight children and family centers to save £8m. The protest drew more than 500 people, including a call for Prime Minister David Cameron to join, as he expressed disappointment with the cuts earlier. The council maintains that it will support vulnerable families, while the government maintains that there is scope for savings across local government.

A sandcastle depicting a sprawled crime victim with large breasts and a large bottom, created by Devon and Cornwall Police during a beach games competition, sparked controversy for its poor taste, offensive imagery, and trivialization of serious matters, particularly for its inappropriateness for a family event and its potential promotion of sexual stereotypes. The force later apologized for any offense caused.

The new owner of Leyton Orient has taken control of the club, and manager Justin Slade anticipates changes to the club's structure, seeking support from the owner and sporting director to strengthen the squad, with the goal to improve upon their performance in the current season and hopefully gain promotion.

Tom Hatton, a 24-year-old golfer from Buckinghamshire, secured a spot at The Open Championship, USPGA at Baltusrol, and achieved his best European Tour finish of outright second with a prize payday of over €429,000, despite missing birdie chances on the back nine at the Scottish Open, where he also won £150,000 more due to a crucial putt on the final green. His main goal at Royal Troon is to make it through the weekend.

The 10-year-old Irish-bred horse, Many Clouds, suffered a rare severe pulmonary haemorrhage and collapsed after winning the Cotswold Chase at Cheltenham's Festival Trials Day, despite no significant underlying health issues, leaving the racing community determined to better understand this illness.

The12-year-old witness testified in Sheffield Crown Court that she was abused by Basharat Hussain and other men, and later forced into prostitution in Blackpool, while being taken out for a meal by Hussain and others initially. Seven individuals, including Basharat Hussain, Arshid Hussain, Qurban Ali, Majid Bostan, Sajid Bostan, Karen MacGregor, and Shelley Davies, are on trial over alleged child abuse in Rotherham, with the accused facing charges ranging from indecent assault to rape.

A 32-year-old racing cyclist, Franck Petricola, sadly passed away in an accident during the practice week of the TT race in the Isle of Man, marking the 141st fatality at the races since their inception in 1907. Petricola had recovered from a serious accident at last year's North West 200 and showed remarkable determination to compete again on the mountain course. The organizers, fellow racers, and those in the road racing community expressed their sympathy for Petricola's family and friends.

Despite cancellation of his much-anticipated return to the Isle of Man TT due to mechanical issues faced by his Honda Racing team this year, the event will still feature top riders like Peter Hickman, Michael Dunlop, and Dean Harrison.

President Barack Obama has declared Louisiana a disaster area due to devastating floods, which have left over 20,000 people rescued and tens of thousands displaced in Baton Rouge, with many still trapped in their homes. Rivers in Louisiana and Mississippi are overflowing, causing widespread destruction. The flood of 2016 is being called "epic" and could rival the devastation of Hurricane Katrina in 2005.

US Soccer has introduced new safety measures for children aged 11-13 in response to a concussion lawsuit, including limiting the amount of heading in practice and modifying substitution rules related to concussions.

Former presidential campaign deputy director Jerome Lavrilleux stated that President Sarkozy, UMP Chairman Jean-Francois Cope, and Bygmalion founder Batien Millot were not aware of accusations of almost 11m euros ($15m; Â£9m) worth of fake invoices during Sarkozy's 2012 campaign.

The number of homes repossessed decreased in the second quarter of 2021 (2,500) compared to the previous quarter and the same quarter in 2020 (5,400), according to the Council of Mortgage Lenders. The decrease is attributed to low interest rates. Lenders caution borrowers to prepare for future interest rate increases. The number of tenants evicted by landlords has risen, raising concerns for renters amid potential future struggles.

From October 2014 to March, the city of Coventry accepted 105 refugees as part of the UK's Syrian Vulnerable Persons Resettlement Scheme, with some having significant medical needs. The UKIP MEP for the West Midlands, James Carver, criticized the distribution of refugees, stating that it is unfair for Coventry to take more refugees than other local authorities. The UK Government is responsible for covering all costs associated with the resettlement programme.

Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff asserts that the 2016 Rio Olympics will bring honor and pride to the country, with the Olympic torch relay kicking off in May 2016 in Brasilia, traveling through 300 cities in 90-100 days, before ending at Rio's Maracana stadium at the Olympics' opening ceremony. Rousseff promises the event will be secure and successful, addressing concerns about delays, pollution, and health risks.

Italian Prime Minister Matteo Renzi's electoral reform package, approved by the lower house of parliament, guarantees a majority of seats to the party with the most votes in elections, aims to end Italy's post-war era of revolving governments, and awards 340 out of 630 seats to parties securing more than 40% of the national vote. The measure provides for a second-round run-off if no party reaches this threshold, and critics argue that it concentrates power in the hands of single parties and denies voters the opportunity to directly select representatives. Opposition parties boycotted the vote. Renzi also seeks to abolish the Senate and replace it with a weaker, non-elected body to further transform the Italian system.

The 20-year-old football player Abdelhak Nouri, while playing for Ajax against Werder Bremen, experienced cardiac arrhythmias, and post-examination suggests he is continuously losing brain function due to a lack of oxygen supply, with recovery prospects being grim.

Swansea secured an important 2-1 victory at Villa Park with goals from Sigurdsson and Ayew, improving morale ahead of their home game with Arsenal and potentially marking a turning point after a six-game losing streak. Sigurdsson believes the team can now meet the targets set for the season.

A Polish mother named Leyla Dad, using the middle name Paulina, is searching for her son Mani Dad, believed to be in the UK with his British father Zayn Dean, and is pleading with Costa coffee shop employees and customers to help find him, as he frequently visited these establishans when the family lived in England. The family had previously resided in Kettering, Northamptonshire, and Bedford before moving to Poland. Leyla launched family court proceedings to locate her son and has asked anyone with information to contact the police.

Dual citizens of Iran, Iraq, Syria, and Sudan, including a BBC presenter, are facing travel restrictions to the US under new visa rules, which they deem unfair due to ambiguity in implementation advice and potential impact on families. The rules were implemented following increased security concerns post Paris attacks, drawing criticism from European diplomats.

Sky is working to resolve capacity issues at specific telephone exchanges, mainly affecting Doncaster, North Wales, and Bristol, to improve service for users with slower internet speeds during peak times. Less than 5% of Sky's broadband customer base are using the affected exchanges. Sky experienced similar issues in some of its exchanges last year, and other service providers have also dealt with similar problems. The issues are due to increased network traffic and high new customer addition rates.

Three individuals, whose ages were not specified, were part of a gang who targeted ATMs in various Scottish locations between August and November 2013, using oxygen and acetylene to blow up the cash machines and steal significant amounts of money. The investigation uncovered their activities due to Scottish banknotes bearing traces of red dye being circulated in the Mersey area. Joseph McHale, Kevin Schruyers, and Robin Vaughan, residents of Liverpool, were all convicted of various crimes, including blowing up cash machines in Aberdeen, New Deer, and other locations, and stealing £112,000, £21,020, and attempting to steal from other locations. Their sentencing was deferred.

Scottish Prison Service will implement mobile phone signal interference technology in two pilot prisons (HMP Shotts and Glenochil) to prevent prisoners from using contraband phones, following legislation allowing such interference. This move aims to address the problems of drug supply, organized crime, and harassment linked to mobile phone use in prisons. The technology is scheduled to be operational within weeks.

French President Francois Hollande participated in a ceremony at a former Nazi camp in Alsace to commemorate the 70th anniversary of its liberation, where he highlighted the importance of knowledge as a means of preventing future atrocities, while the ongoing surge of attacks on Jews and Muslims in France has reignited debate about social tensions, and similar commemorative events took place in Germany, Israel, and Croatia for other liberated Nazi camps, including Bergen-Belsen and Jasenovac.

Actor Johnny Depp and his wife Amber Heard are divorcing after a months-long legal case in Australia stemming from her illegal importation of two dogs in 2015. The separation occurred after Depp's mother's death and the release of his latest film, Alice Through the Looking Glass. The legal case was settled with a video apology.

A container ship, Maersk Tigris, with 24 crew members, mostly from Eastern Europe and Asia, remains boarded off Bandar Abbas, Iran, after being seized by Iranian authorities on suspicion of debt-related issues from a private Iranian company. The ship, under charter from Singapore-based Rickmers Shipmanagement, was carrying commercial goods and not military equipment, and reported a distress call while navigating through waters under international agreement open to foreign ships. The U.S. Navy dispatched a destroyer and a reconnaissance plane to monitor the situation, with a Pentagon spokesman calling the actions of the Iranian Revolutionary Guards Navy patrol vessels, who ordered the ship to go deeper into Iranian waters then fired warning shots, as "inappropriate."

A request to disclose the full investigation report on the 2012 suicide of 14-year-old foster child Seren Bernard in Pembrokeshire was denied by the council, leaving the girl's mother, Sarah Pollock, feeling traumatized and out of answers for unanswered questions, despite the report being deemed a "document for learning".

In the final match of the Super League regular season, Leigh defeated Salford, securing Widnes' position at the bottom of the table while missing out on a chance to achieve their highest league position in 40 years. Leigh's victory was marked by a strong defensive effort and effective game management, while Salford struggled to meet their usual standards. Leigh coach Neil Jukes praised his team's performance, citing good defensive effort, game management, and minimal penalties as keys to the victory. Salford coach Ian Watson acknowledged a poor display, attributing the drop in intensity to their post-top-eight finish slump.

Paul Allen, aided by Burt Rutan and Elon Musk, is developing Stratolaunch Systems, a giant aircraft to launch unmanned rockets into orbit from high-flying aircraft, with plans for manned missions and satellite delivery; plans include the use of a space company owned by Musk, and the first test flights are scheduled for 2016, after 10 years of preliminary designs.

Despite Lancashire establishing a significant 264-run lead in the match thanks to Alex Davies' impressive 89, Derbyshire manage to dismiss their openers, ending the day on 27-2 at the mercy of Lancashire's bowlers, with Peter Siddle and Tom Bailey claiming the wickets, as Davies and Jarvis had earlier contributed a valuable 160-run partnership during Lancashire's innings.

Jon Stewart, known as a prominent American satirist and host of The Daily Show on Comedy Central, bid farewell to the program after 16 years, with notable guests such as Bruce Springsteen, US Secretary of State John Kerry, and Senator John McCain. He will be replaced by Trevor Noah, while the show continues to be a significant news source for young audiences, having launched the careers of several comedians such as John Oliver and Steve Carell. #JonVoyage trended on Twitter as celebrities paid tribute.

Forest, who have won the cup four times and last featured in European competition in the 1995-96 season, will start their campaign in the third round of the cup competition against League Two side Doncaster, while their goalkeeper Dorus de Vries is expected to be out for a few weeks due to an injury sustained in the season opener.

The Arches nightclub has gone into administration and could potentially affect 130 jobs, following a midnight closure ruling due to drug abuse and disorder concerns. The Scottish Government has pledged support, with Creative Scotland offering financial assistance and exploring options for the venue's future.

A 77-year-old, Ivor Bell, a former senior Provisional IRA leader, was arrested in connection with the abduction, murder, and secret burial of Jean McConville, one of the "Disappeared" in Northern Ireland during the Troubles, and is expected to appear in court on charges of aiding and abetting murder and IRA membership.

Wigan Warriors came back from a disadvantage of 12 men following a red card and scored 21 unanswered points to beat Warrington Wolves, boosting their chances of securing a home semi-final in their upcoming game against Catalans Dragons. However, their hopes of clinching the League Leaders' Shield are slim.

The Yorkshire Sculpture Park experienced a 170% increase in visitor numbers in September, with 100,000 people visiting to see the poppy installation; expecting its highest visitor numbers ever, with over half a million visitors, and the poppy installation creating a calm and contemplative experience for many.

The A361 between East Lyng and Burrowbridge was closed due to a flood warning and reopened on March 10th with temporary traffic lights, after inspections and cleanup operations. The A372 Langport Road will remain closed for flood pump removal next week, after which the A361 will be assessed for flood damage and undergo emergency repairs.

A newly discovered object, V774104, observed by Japan's Subaru telescope, is estimated to be approximately 500-1,000 km across and currently about three times further from the Sun than Pluto, making it the most distant known solar system object as of now. Scientists, including Scott Sheppard and Chad Trujillo, are examining its orbit to determine whether it follows an inward or outward trajectory, comparable to objects like Eris, 2012 VP113, and Sedna. The team specializes in detecting solar system outliers, and the object's potential origins range from being perturbed by a passing planet to being stolen from a star in the same "nursery" as the Sun.

Ashley Yates, a former head teacher at The Tynings Primary School in Staple Hill, South Gloucestershire, has admitted charges of making indecent images of children and voyeurism. The crime involved filming six girls, one boy, and two staff members using a spy pen. The police have confirmed that additional adult victims have been identified and are offering support to them. The school is working closely with the police and the local authority to provide information without compromising the legal proceedings.

Great Britain's rowing team, consisting of Helena Glover and Heather Stanning, dominated the Women's Pair event in the Rio Olympics, winning gold with a new record time of 7 minutes 18.29 seconds. They have now won 39 consecutive races, including the 2012 London Games title. The win comes as they defended their Olympic title, with Stanning stating that this victory means much more than their London success due to the increased pressure as they were defending a title, as well as Pixie Lott, Dan Walker, and Polly Swann expressing praise for the athlete's performance.

Steve and Ola, participants on Strictly Come Dancing, have faced unfounded bullying allegations in the media. Despite the negative attention, they have chosen not to engage with the claims and instead have focused on their performances, maintaining their unity as a team. They emphasized that such accusations were not a true reflection of their experience on the show and reminded viewers to consider the source of such reports before forming judgments. They also referred readers to resources offering help for those affected by bullying.

The article reports that inflation dropped to 2.6% in June from 2.9%, leading to a decline in the value of the pound against both the U.S. dollar and the euro. The drop in inflation lowered expectations for an immediate interest rate hike, but it may not completely rule out one happening later in the year if conditions improve. The downturn in the pound initially boosted the FTSE 100 share index but ended the day down 13.91 points, while Royal Mail shares rose 3% due to a 1% increase in revenues.

Actress Vicky McClure, whose tram on the Nottingham city network is named after her, experienced a misunderstanding when a conductor approached her and her mother and asked for their tickets despite being offered a free ride after the ceremony to honor her.

The inquest into the death of 14-year-old Alice Gross, found dead in the River Brent in west London in September 2014, will examine potential government and police failings related to the case of a convicted murderer who was a suspect in her death but died before being charged.

The Local Data Company and the University of Stirling's research shows that Scotland's average retail vacancy rate decreased from 14.5% to 13.7%, with East Kilbride having the highest vacancy rate and Inverurie the lowest. Nearly 40% of empty stores have been vacant for more than three years, and town vacancy rates improved at twice the rate of cities. The report highlights the growing significance of leisure businesses in towns and cities, with Aberdeen having the highest proportion of charity shops in a city, and Penicuik in Midlothian having the greatest proportion of charity shops in a town. Matthew Hopkinson of the Local Data Company comments on the findings, stating that the high proportion of long-term vacancies indicates a major barrier to healthy and sustainable communities.

Rory McWhirter fraudulently obtained personal details from individuals for fake job applications, securing marriage certificates to register fictitious births, and ultimately claimed over £34,000 in welfare benefits. Caught due to returning to an early registration location and recognized, he was sentenced to imprisonment for the complex fraud.

The authorities are attempting to demolish Awamiya's old quarter, a predominantly Shia area in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia, causing violence, displacement, and accusations of human rights abuses against the Shia population who claim marginalization and discrimination by the Sunni monarchy. The unrest escalated following the execution of Shia cleric Nimr al-Nimr in 2016, and the disputed executions and bombings in the region since then.

The article discusses the struggles of young people in Belfast, specifically aged 18, to find employment, and their criticisms of the political landscape in Northern Ireland, where they perceive the politicians to be more focused on personal gain during election times, rather than addressing issues related to job opportunities, drug reform, and health care when not campaigning.

Barnet Council's Chief Executive, Andrew Travers, left the council after voters were turned away from all 155 polling stations due to missing names on the poll list, and a subsequent independent investigation will be launched to review the appropriateness of arrangements for the EU Referendum.

Manager Neil Warnock has given Peter Whittingham ample time to consider a new contract offer, while seeking alternative arrangements for midfielders Emyr Huws and Stuart O'Keefe, who are not part of his long-term plans for the football team.

A BBC and BuzzFeed News investigation has revealed suspected match-fixing in tennis, with tennis player Jamie Murray expressing concern over the difficulty of proving match-fixing and assuring spectators at the Australian Open that the matches are pure and fair. The article does not specify at what level the suspected match-fixing was taking place.

A 60-year-old man, suspected of producing a firearm but without making threats or demands, surrendered to police after holding a female staff member hostage in a bank interview room on Bristol Road South, Northfield. No customers were harmed during the incident.

A British computer software programmer, Mohammed Ali, is on trial in London for allegedly trying to purchase the deadly toxin ricin online. The FBI intercepted the deal during an investigation, with the agent posing as a dealer. The defense argues that Ali's actions were motivated by his interest in the television series "Breaking Bad" and that he has traits consistent with Asperger's syndrome. The trial continues.

Newport County is facing criticism following recent abandoned games at Rodney Parade due to a poor pitch condition, with Chief Executive Darren Davies defending the lease agreement, stating that the cost of maintenance outweighs the revenue received from the football club.

Approximately 69% of the surveyed individuals admitted to working while unwell, primarily due to fear of accumulating work, while 23% falsely claimed sick days. The report suggests this practice, known as presenteeism, can be detrimental to business performance due to lower productivity and morale.

The British pound declined against both the US dollar and the euro, while the FTSE 100 index closed marginally up, driven by mining shares. Notable falls included Hikma, down 8.2%, due to regulatory delays for a new drug, Centrica, down 5.4%, due to concerns over regulation and potential price wars, and BT, down 4.5%, following a drop in annual profits.

Russian hacker Roman Seleznev, son of a Russian MP, was found guilty of stealing nearly 3 million credit card numbers from US pizza chains in Washington state over six years, with 3,700 businesses affected. He faces a four-year mandatory prison sentence following the trial, with plans for an appeal against his conviction on grounds of an illegal arrest and misuse of evidence. The US authorities maintain that Seleznev was prosecuted for his actions, not his nationality, while Russia has lodged complaints about his seizure and extradition.

The individual stated that he does not possess any recordings as suggested in a tweet following his firing of James Comey, who had been investigating alleged Russian interference in the election and potential links to the Trump team. The tweet was in response to alleged requests from the president to drop an investigation and for assurances of loyalty.

Liberty, led by Sanjeev Gupta, plans to submit a letter of intent for a bid to acquire Tata Steel's assets, including the UK's largest steelworks in Port Talbot, as well as sites at Newport, Rotherham, Corby, Shotton, and Teesside, on Tuesday. The management buyout team Excalibur Steel UK Limited is also planning a bid for the business, and Tata's Scunthorpe operation, which employs more than 3,000 people, has been sold to investment firm Greybull Capital. Macquarie, the Australian bank, is being considered as a potential financial backer of any takeover. Liberty specializes in recycling scrap metal rather than producing steel in blast furnaces, and has reached deals for steel plants in Newport, the Black Country, and Lanarkshire in recent years. The government has pledged support for any potential buyers of the business, offering a stake and financial assistance.

The East Midlands region's 19 councils have identified expanding the Nottingham tram network to East Midlands Airport and Toton's HS2 station as a priority project to efficiently connect cities like Derby, with past estimates placing the cost of a new tram line at approximately £20m per mile. The cost of individual proposed links, such as from Toton to Derby and from Nottingham to Ripley, was estimated at around £200m and £180m, respectively, based on past evaluations. The broader strategic transport initiatives that the East Midlands councils aim to negotiate with the government are not yet specified.

Ronnie O'Sullivan, the five-time world champion, claimed a record-equalling 9-0 Masters victory, attributing his success to altering his game and placing emphasis on mental fortitude amid physical difficulties, which has bolstered his self-confidence for future competitions like the World Championship.

The devastating weekend storms in Poland resulted in six fatalities, extensive property damage, and the felling of over eight million cubic meters of lumber across 45,000 hectares of forest, particularly affecting areas like Torun, Gdansk, and Poznan. The incident is said to be the worst forest disaster in Polish (and possibly European) history. The disaster occurs as the Polish government faces criticism for logging in Europe's oldest forest, Bialowieza, a UNESCO World Heritage site, where destructive bark beetle infestation is cited as justification for logging, despite opposition from Unesco, EU officials, and green activists. The European Court of Justice will determine if the logging ban remains in place, with potential multimillion euro fines if Poland is found in violation.

Singer Enrique Iglesias was injured at a concert in Tijuana, Mexico when he tried to grab a drone camera and needed reconstructive surgery, but the injury is not expected to prevent him from resuming his tour on 3 July after a few weeks of recovery.

Leeds Rhinos beat Warrington Wolves 28-0 in the Super League match, with Matt Parcell scoring three tries and Joel Moon scoring his 15th try of the season. Leeds moved up to third in Super League with their fifth win in seven games.

William (Plum) Smith, who spent a decade in prison for a 1972 shooting and played a crucial role in the 1994 ceasefire of loyalist paramilitary groups, was remembered for his significant contributions to peace efforts and his negotiations with traditional enemies, as highlighted by Martin McGuinness and Brian Ervine.

Olive Cooke, a 92-year-old Bristol resident and long-standing Royal British Legion (RBL) poppy seller, has been promoting the remembrance of World War I and II heroes for over 75 years, particularly highlighting the sacrifice of her late husband, Leslie Hussey-Yeo, who was killed in action in 1943. The RBL categorizes Mrs. Cooke as their "most-valued poppy collector" for her past 12 years of service, primarily selling poppies at the entrance of Bristol Cathedral.

Shimon Peres, a prominent Israeli politician who served twice as prime minister, once as president, and played key roles in Israel's defense and defense procurement, passed away after a major stroke, following a long career advocating for peace with the Palestinians. Widely mourned by political leaders worldwide, he continued to be active in promoting peace through his Peres Centre for Peace.

A major survey at Queen's University, involving a large portion of the staff, reveals low ratings for leadership and change management, but high levels of personal pride, work interest, and overall positive sentiments. The university acknowledges the results and plans to collaborate with staff to address pain points and develop action plans for improvement.

The X-47B jet, a tailless, stealthy unmanned aircraft developed by Northrop Grumman for the US Navy, successfully completed its maiden flight, marking a significant step towards a new era of high-speed, radar-evading drones; scheduled for further testing in 2013, before potential aircraft carrier deployment.

Airbus has decided to produce fewer A380 planes due to lack of demand and is planning to introduce an improved version in hopes of attracting more sales, while facing delays in engine deliveries for the A320neo from Pratt & Whitney which results in marginal losses. Airbus is also in talks with Qatar Airways about cancelling orders for A350 planes.

Nearly 40% of coral has died at the Dongsha Atoll in the South China Sea due to a spike in temperatures caused by a high-pressure system, and experts warn that a 2-degree Celsius cap on ocean warming may not be enough to save such coral reefs, particularly in shallow water where a local weather change can lead to higher temperatures and more severe impacts.

Researchers have discovered a protein named Hi1a in the venom of Australian funnel-web spiders, which has shown potential in preventing brain damage in lab rats after a stroke by blocking acid-sensing ion channels, a key driver of brain damage after a stroke. The research is still in its early stages and has yet to undergo human trials.

Oldham took an early lead through an unchallenged header from Peter Clarke but Bradford dominated play for much of the game and eventually equalized through a penalty in the second half, resulting in a 1-1 draw.

Experts have expressed cautious optimism for the drug aducanumab, which showed promise in halting memory decline and reducing amyloid plaques in a small study, but concern remains due to side effects and past failures in Alzheimer's drug development, as larger phase 3 trials with 2,700 patients are now underway.

Lowly Oldham Roughyeds pulled off a stunning upset in the Challenge Cup, defeating Super League side Hull KR 24-28, with star player Richard Lepori scoring two tries. The result was particularly significant for Oldham, who are in their first season in the second tier of the championship, while Hull KR, who are one of the top tiers, have struggled this season with only two wins in Super League. After the match, Hull KR coach James Webster described his team's performance as an "utter embarrassment," while Oldham's coach Scott Naylor hailed it as one of the biggest wins in the club's history.

The BBC's director general, Tony Hall, has announced plans for the corporation to modernize for the internet age, including a children's iPlayer, local reporters, and the Ideas Service platform. Funding cuts may necessitate the closure or reduction of some current services. The aim is to co-operate with cultural institutions and companies in a global media landscape, but local news providers have raised concerns about the proposed partnership with newspapers.

The Equality and Human Rights Commission has written to political leaders expressing concern over an increase in hate attacks since the UK's EU referendum, including racist, anti-Semitic, and homophobic attacks. The commission calls for "accurate information and respectful debate," and urges politicians to recognize and address the widening divisions in society. The letter also criticizes government policies that may contribute to these tensions, such as the proposed plan to require companies to disclose the proportion of foreign workers they employ. The commission suggests a review of sentences for hate crimes and calls for more concerted action to address the issue.

Ms. Evans, a former UKIP policy maker who wrote the party's 2015 general election manifesto, is suspended from the party after being found to have publicly criticized a fellow candidate and held herself out as a party spokeswoman without authority. She is unable to run for leadership due to a few individuals at the top preventing her. She has endorsed councillor Lisa Duffy to succeed Nigel Farage and called for UKIP to set itself firmly "in the common sense centre-ground" and conduct internal reforms.

In England, a new grading system will replace traditional letters with numbers (1-9), and coursework will be eliminated for most subjects starting with students taking GCSEs in 2017. The changes in curriculum and assessment format are intended to improve core skills in maths and English, with a focus on deep learning, grammar, spelling, and punctuation. The reforms are scheduled to begin in autumn 2015 for English language, English literature, and maths, with other subjects being revised over the following year. Similar changes are being considered in Wales, but Northern Ireland and Scotland are not making any changes to their existing examination systems.

Retired Gen. David Petraeus, who faced a scandal for sharing classified material with his biographer, indicated a willingness to serve under Trump if asked, and suggested Trump's diplomatic approach to Russia could resemble Nixon's overtures to China in the 1970s.

A summary of the article describes a recent meeting between Hillary Clinton and newly elected President Mohammed Mursi of Egypt, during which Clinton urged compromise and praised the role of Egypt's military council during their interim leadership. The meeting was aimed at stabilizing Egypt's fledgling democracy and addressing various issues such as Mursi's attempts to reinstate the parliament, the military's return to a purely military role, and the protection of women's rights and minorities, as well as the peace treaty with Israel. Clinton also plans to meet with Field Marshal Mohammed Hussein Tantawi, Egypt's interim ruler, the next day.

Derek Bruder, a 1989 disaster survivor, testified in the recent inquests that he was asked by West Midlands Police inspector Matthew Sawers to make changes to his statement about the final movements of a victim he had tried to resuscitate, who ultimately died. Sawers denies attempting to change Bruder's statement, insisting he sought only to gather more detail and explanation. The inquests are ongoing.

The article discusses how musician Josephine Vander Gucht of Oh Wonder wrote the upbeat and energetic song "High on Humans" after encountering a bloodied stranger on a train, which inspired her to write about the power of human connection. The song is not explicitly stated as being included in the upcoming second album "Ultralife", but the album is set for release in July. The producer, Anthony West, hopes to write about "the human experience" in this day and age on the album.

Chelsea's Bertrand Traore opened the scoring with a goal from Nemanja Matic's pass, but Stoke City responded with a header from Xherdan Shaqiri's cross. Diego Costa and Cesc Fabregas were not in the squad due to injuries.

William C Campbell, Satoshi Omura, and Youyou Tu's research has led to the development of life-changing drugs (ivermectin, artemisinin) to combat diseases like malaria, river blindness (onchocerciasis), and elephantiasis (lympatic filariasis), affecting over 3.4 billion people globally. These treatments are the results of discoveries originating from bacteria found in a Japanese golf course, traditional Chinese medicine, and ancient literature.

The Nelson Mandela Foundation has called on the African National Congress to hold South African President Zuma accountable for corruption allegations and potential misuse of state resources, as investigations into his dealings with the Gupta family continue, potentially leading to impeachment or corruption trial proceedings, according to the article. The Foundation has expressed concern that these actions threaten South Africa's democracy.

British comedian and actress Miranda did a trademark gallop during the curtain call at Annie, a West End musical at London's Piccadilly Theatre, where she plays the role of the unconventional orphanage owner, Miss Hannigan. The musical's optimism and ability to cheer people up was highlighted in response to recent terror attacks, and it will be running at the Piccadilly Theatre until 6th January 2018.

A 23-year-old midfielder, Jonjo Shelvey, scored the assist in both goals as Newcastle United secured their first league win in five games against West Ham United, with a final score of 2-1. The victory moved them out of the relegation zone. The article highlights Shelvey's impressive performance.

Diesel prices in the UK dropped below average petrol prices due to cheaper wholesale diesel costs and increased supply from refineries outside the UK, potentially resulting in diesel prices lower by up to 4p per litre compared to petrol over the next fortnight, according to RAC fuel spokesman Simon Williams.

Africa's 70th UN General Assembly is a critical meeting place for leaders to engage in international cooperation to address ongoing conflicts, humanitarian crises, and issues like hunger and economic instability in Africa, with a particular focus on ending hunger as part of the Sustainable Development Goals. The UN remains a crucial lifeline for vulnerable populations across the continent.

Superman-logo pills containing the harmful substance PMMA may still be in circulation, warns the police, with Dr Adam Winstock suggesting the pills may have originated from the Netherlands and are often mistaken for MDMA. He advises staying hydrated, monitoring friends' safety, using home testing kits cautiously, and seeking immediate medical attention if concerned about a drug's effects. He also suggests that a small group test a small amount of the drug before taking a full dose together.

A Leave.EU campaign chairman has proposed that UKIP's leader re-engage former leader Nigel Farage, hire a CEO from industry, install a new team of trained agents, and draw up new policies, while ousting a faction of allegedly unhelpful senior figures, according to a letter to the current leader. UKIP's MEP and principal political adviser criticized this recommendation, emphasizing that donors should not dictate party affairs.

Invisible Girlfriend is a service that allows users to create a virtual girlfriend for $15-$25 a month. The service provides text messages from real humans and is popular, with over 60% of accounts choosing boyfriends. Users often use the service to maintain personal or social situations, such as getting parents off their back or making an ex-jealous. The service is viewed by some as a source of companionship rather than a sad or pathetic choice.

Germany showcased a dominant offensive performance in a 2-0 victory over Poland, with Thomas Muller, Karim Bellarabi, Bastian Schweinsteiger, and Mario Gotze excelling. However, the German defense showed vulnerabilities that Scotland may exploit in their upcoming match.

In the Championship, Blackburn Rovers and Bristol City drew 1-1, with both teams creating numerous chances throughout the game; Rovers remain two points from safety with three games left, while Bristol City are four points above the relegation zone, as of half-time. Additionally, on-loan Chelsea striker Tammy Abraham had the best opportunity for Bristol City but struck straight at the goalkeeper.

Scotland aims to send off outgoing coach Gregor Townsend's successor, Vern Cotter, with a victory over Ireland in the opening Six Nations match, despite Ireland's significant advantage in previous championship encounters. The Scottish team, led by number eight Strauss, aspires to give their coach a great send-off due to the emotional incentive it provides. Ireland's aggressive play, particularly in the set-piece, and the form of stand-out player CJ Stander, pose significant challenges for Scotland. However, Scotland's resource coach, Nathan Hines, expects Ireland to identify and exploit Scottish weaknesses, urging Scotland to combat this effectively. Ireland captain Rory Best acknowledges the inexperience of Scotland's front-row in Test rugby but praises their strong performances domestically, expecting a difficult match.

Celtic's John Guidetti scores a free-kick following a red card to Pascali for a professional foul on Scepovic, Kilmarnock's goalkeeper Conor Brennan makes several impressive saves but cannot prevent Scepovic from scoring a second after the break in a one-sided second half. Celtic replace Scepovic and Johansen with Griffiths and Mulgrew, respectively, and move up to fourth in the Scottish Premiership with the win.

Northern Irish pupils have life satisfaction scores close to the average of 7.3, but concerns over exam anxiety, bullying, and heavy internet usage remain issues for many, despite high levels of engagement with parents and teachers, and academic ambition, which can lead to more satisfaction. The findings are based on a global survey of 540,000 students, including those in Northern Ireland.

Crystal Palace overcame Everton 3-2 after a comeback from 1-0 down, with Romelu Lukaku's goal canceled out by a Mile Jedinak penalty, a Fraizer Campbell header, and a Yannick Bolasie low shot. Neil Warnock's tactically astute Crystal Palace showed resilience and self-belief against an initially dominant Everton side.

Freelance sports journalist Gary Carter, aged 36, was found with head injuries in Bethnal Green early on Friday morning following an altercation. His wife Gemma stated that he was heavily sedated while waiting for the swelling on his brain to subside. A 35-year-old man, James Flanagan, was charged with causing grievous bodily harm. The case is currently under investigation by Scotland Yard. Carter, who regularly works for The Sun, was in London to cover a rugby league match between England and New Zealand. His colleagues in the sport and on social media, including Alan Shearer, sent him well-wishes for a full recovery.

British rapper Tinie Tempah, who holds the record for the most number one singles in this decade by a British artist, discusses his second home studio, where he recorded his million-selling debut and is currently working on his third album, Youth. He shares how he struggled to balance fame and staying true to his roots, ultimately finding inspiration by reconnecting with old friends. This new album, set to release on April 14, is categorized by a playfulness and warmth missing from his previous work. Tempah also credits the recent success of grime as a genre, specifically artists like Skepta and the genre's "uninvited" history.

Mobile operators, including O2, are seeking a faster allocation of spectrum by the communications regulator Ofcom, aiming for an earlier launch of 4G networks in the UK compared to EE, which had previously been given permission to offer 4G services. This effort may be influenced by legal challenges, negotiations, and competition from Apple's iPhone 5, with the networks hoping for a more competitive pricing strategy to attract customers.

The Conservative Party has discontinued a policy of offering free school lunches to children in the first three years of primary school, leading to criticism from teachers and unions who believe it will affect children's overall nutrition, particularly those from low-income families. The policy has been criticized for being costly, with many schools needing to upgrade their kitchen facilities before it could be implemented.

A shooting incident took place in a busy area of Tel Aviv's city center on Dizengoff Street, leaving four seriously injured. Israeli security forces have launched a massive manhunt to find the gunman, whose identity and motive remains unclear. The shooting occurred during the peak of the weekend on Friday afternoon. Police spokesman Micky Rosenfeld stated that there was no specific warning of an attack, and it remains unclear if the incident is terrorism- or crime-related.

Ambrose Salvonna, a lion tamer buried in Inverness, was discovered by family researcher Judi Menabney, who found his grave with help from Highland Archive and Registration Centre staff. The discovery revealed Ambrose to be a colorful and popular figure in Highland town, and inspired singer Dean Owens' song "Dora," about his grandmother who grew up in Salvonna's circus.

At Glastonbury 2021, sustainably-sourced recycled steel pint cups are introduced on a major scale for the first time. However, they are not compulsory and not all bars offer them. Their awkward shape and lack of a logo make them difficult to throw as missiles, unlike recyclable plastic cups. The cups are intended to be part of a reusable revolution, aiming to reduce waste and promote British steel industry. The festival organizers opted for stainless steel over plastic due to the toxic substances released during plastic glass production and the environmentally harmful nature of plastic waste.

A 15-year-old boy survived the earthquake by drinking water from wet clothes and eating clarified butter, while a woman in her 20s was rescued after being trapped for over 8 hours. The rescue effort involves teams from various countries, but relief efforts are being hampered by bad weather and difficulties reaching remote areas. Many survivors are falling ill due to contaminated water, and the death toll has risen to 6,130 with over 13,000 injured. Climbing on Mount Everest is expected to resume next week, and, despite extensive damage, the number of casualties in many villages was lower than feared due to people working outside when the quake struck.

JP Morgan plans to potentially relocate between 500 and 1,000 staff to Dublin, Frankfurt, Luxembourg, Paris, Milan, Madrid, and Stockholm as part of contingency plans for Brexit, following similar announcements from various financial services companies regarding the movement of staff out of London.

The article states that police in Ferguson broke up a crowd after a curfew started, a police car was shot at, and a person was injured in an unrelated shooting. The shooting of 18-year-old black teenager Michael Brown by a white policeman on August 9 has sparked allegations of police brutality in the primarily black suburb of Ferguson, leading to protests and riots. The officer who shot Brown was identified as Darren Wilson, a six-year police veteran with no prior complaints. The shooting is being investigated by the US justice department and territorial authorities are working to restore peace.

Diane Abbott, the Labour shadow home secretary, accused Theresa May of allowing a decrease in police officer numbers during May's tenure as home secretary and suggested this may have contributed to recent terrorist attacks, while the Conservatives stated that armed police numbers have increased and a former terrorism law watchdog argued that cuts in community policing are not directly linked to terrorism.

The world champions, New Zealand, routed Wales 46-6, marking their 29th consecutive win and Wales' heaviest loss in 9 years. Welsh coach Warren Gatland sees numerous lessons for his team from this defeat and aims to improve on them when they meet again, while New Zealand coach Steve Hansen attributes Wales' performance to the end of their long season.

Five individuals, including a 17-year-old British boy named Stephen Thomas who was a talented photographer and a driving force behind the Swindon Down's Syndrome Group, died in a boat accident in Canada. The incident happened on the open, upper deck of the boat where the victims were not wearing life jackets. The Canadian government is investigating the cause of the accident, and officials suggest the rapid response from the local community saved more lives. A 27-year-old Australian man is still missing, and his girlfriend and her family were on board when the boat sank.

The article describes a signing ceremony of a ceasefire agreement by several armed groups in Myanmar (Burma), which President Thein Sein said broke new ground toward a future of peace, but notably excluded key groups including the largest, the United Wa State Army (UWSA), and the Kachin Independence Organisation (KIO). The government aims to continue negotiations with the non-signing groups for political discussions on a new, likely more federal system of government, with concerns for short-lived peace if the Burmese army fails to adhere to the ceasefire, as it has in the past.

Facebook was ordered to remove a page targeting a Northern Irish man with a history of sexual offenses from the 1980s, as it amounted to harassment and a potential violation of his human rights. The man sought an interim injunction and damages from Facebook Ireland Ltd, citing threats to his safety. While the court upheld the interim order, it emphasized that it did not suppress information about the man's criminal record already in the public domain. The judge also acknowledged the case's sensitivity and reminded that similar cases would be highly fact-dependent.

Apple is due to launch a news app later this year, inviting publishers to participate. The terms of the agreement, sent via email, presume acceptance of the terms unless active opt-out is stated. The terms require publishers to indemnify Apple for legal claims related to RSS content, and allow Apple to place ads next to their content without compensation. This opt-out approach is considered unusual, and some publishers have expressed concerns over the requirement to opt-out.

The article discusses concerns on Guam, a US Pacific territory with a significant US military presence, as residents prepare for potential threat from North Korea. Although the authorities have reassured residents, some have taken precautions, while others are skeptical about immediate military responses. Guam, with its 165,000 civilians, is reportedly just 14-15 minutes away from potential North Korean missile range.

Sentinel-1b was launched into orbit by a Soyuz rocket from French Guiana as part of the European Union's flagship space project, Copernicus, which aims to monitor Earth's health and environment with a multitude of applications, including tracking shipping lanes for pollution and icebergs, and observing land surfaces for signs of subsidence. The satellite will work alongside Sentinel-1a, and along with other upcoming satellites, they will provide an avalanche of data and help with services ranging from air quality updates to infrastructure planning. Additionally, a French space agency mission called Microscope, which aims to investigate the equivalence principle, was flown on the same mission.

The article suggests that the pound may have gained due to the snap election call by Theresa May because markets expect that a larger majority could allow her to negotiate a softer Brexit, potentially reducing economic uncertainty.

A hiker named Pavlina Pizova became stranded on the Routeburn track within Fiordland National Park after getting lost due to bad conditions with her partner Ondrej Petr. Petr later died after slipping on an ice slope, leaving Pizova to spend a night with his body in the open before moving to a hut, where she spent nearly a month alone. She was eventually found by search and rescue teams and is currently in reasonable health.

Elena, a 40-year-old Muscovite, and her husband owe over a million roubles to four banks, putting them just above the poverty line. Millions of Russians are in debt with similar issues paying loans or mortgages. The debt crisis stems from a history of borrowing exacerbated by financial hardship due to the global financial crisis and Western sanctions against Russia.

The Denver court ruled against expanded media coverage of the James Holmes case, while allowing filming of court proceedings, as some victims' families have expressed a desire to limit publicity of the suspect.

The Art Recovery Group, led by Christopher Marinello, is combating the trafficking of looted Syrian antiquities by using the Art Claim database to identify and prevent the sale of such objects with no known provenance, aiming to curb the crisis and prevent funding for terrorism groups like ISIS.

The report, following the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant disaster, found that the loss of life, contamination, and widespread damage were avoidable and a result of systemic failures. These failures included a reluctance to question authority, collusion between regulators, government, and operators, inadequate safety measures, poor emergency response, and insufficient evacuation planning. The report also criticized existing laws and regulations that prioritize nuclear energy promotion over public safety. The disaster was labeled as "man-made" and a "disaster made in Japan," stemming from the country's cultural and organizational flaws.

The article discusses the UK government's auto-enrolment programme, which has seen a 95% compliance rate among small businesses and a focus on enrolling diverse workers such as nannies, care workers, plumbers, and bar staff. There are concerns about the adequacy of contribution levels, with the average employer contribution being 3%, and calls for increased minimum rates to ensure a decent retirement. Additionally, concerns have been raised about certain trusts managing pensions for small firms.

The article summarizes a Canadian-led study published in Nature Geoscience that estimates the total amount of water stored in the top 2km of Earth's surface, with modern groundwater (6%) being quickly renewed, sensitive to climate change, and human contamination, making it a vital resource to manage sustainably. The research also reveals significant variations in the distribution of modern groundwater reserves worldwide.

The European Challenge Cup final for 2017 will be held in Edinburgh, alongside the Champions Cup final, following a successful bid assisted by the Scottish Government and Event Scotland. This decision is a testament to Scotland's passion for rugby and its ability to host world-class events.

Former CIA worker Edward Snowden, wanted by the US over leaks of surveillance programs, remains in Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport's transit zone due to an unresolved asylum application and a lack of travel documents. The White House has not made it clear what further actions it plans regarding Snowden's status in Russia.

Brazil's Attorney-General has asked the Supreme Court to investigate former President Lula for alleged involvement in the Petrobras corruption scandal involving suspicious property transactions and illicit benefits from construction companies in the Petrobras kickback scheme, potentially including obstruction of justice.

Three SAS candidates, L/Cpl Craig Roberts, Cpl James Dunsby, and L/Cpl Edward Maher, died during a selection exercise in Powys on one of the hottest days of 2013 due to heat-related illness. A coroner ruled neglect contributed to their deaths, and the Health and Safety Executive issued a censure for failures by the Ministry of Defence that led to the deaths. But the UK government has rejected calls to remove the MoD's immunity from prosecution under the Corporate Manslaughter Act, stating that existing mechanisms for ensuring lessons are learned and mistakes are not repeated are sufficient. The families of the deceased believe holding the MoD legally accountable would lead to safer training methods.

Leicester City, the reigning Premier League champions, are struggling to avoid relegation and have lost every away match in the Premier League this season, leaving them just one point above the relegation zone and facing criticism from their coach for a lack of fight and team cohesion.

Footballers, entertainers, and clubs are under HMRC investigation for potential irregularities in their tax-related image rights payments into offshore accounts. The HMRC has recovered £158m in the past two years by investigating these issues, with the focus on whether the transfers are genuine, properly valued, and whether income should be returned to the UK based on the individuals' residency status. Allegations of tax avoidance involving individuals like José Mourinho and Cristiano Ronaldo have emerged, but their representatives deny any wrongdoing. The Committee responsible for overseeing government expenditure plans to call the HMRC head for testimony.

The treason investigation into two journalists for publishing classified documents about German intelligence service's online surveillance plans has caused a national debate about freedom of the press, with government leaders withdrawing support for the chief prosecutor, leading to his dismissal. Despite the investigation being suspended, the case continues to raise questions about what constitutes a state secret, what journalists can publish, and the definition of a journalist in the digital age.

The Chancellor's Budget speech pointed to various announcements aimed at stimulating growth in locations across the UK, including Aberdeen, the Midlands, and Ebbsfleet for a new garden city, drawing criticism from political opponents who accuse him of neglecting the South East region.

Despite Colchester United managing to stifle Doncaster Rovers' passing game and arguably having more dangerous chances throughout the match, it was Rovers who snatched a narrow 1-0 win, thanks to Tommy Rowe's goal right before half-time.

In an interview with BBC Newsnight, Ross McEwan, the CEO of Royal Bank of Scotland (RBS), expressed concerns that the unpredictability of the Brexit referendum could slow down businesses, including banks, and anticipated that the Bank of England may not raise interest rates before 2017. The RBS remains owned by the British government after a £45bn bailout in 2008.

Labour and the SNP are the main focus of the article, with Labour being concerned about preserving the UK and promoting a welfare state, while the SNP emphasizes Scottish nationalism and preventing the Conservatives from returning to power. The Scottish Conservatives aim to maintain Scotland's economy and ensure strong leadership, while the Scottish Liberal Democrats prioritize improving mental health services and maintaining a centrist political stance. The article does not provide information on the positions of UKIP or the Liberal Democrats at the national level during the 2015 general election.

University of the West of England students Elliot Vale and Tia Mountain have developed GeoRescue, a conceptual app that aims to provide individuals with real-time information about natural disasters and guide them to safety, using GPS signals and advanced maps services. They will be presenting their idea at a space conference in Manchester and will pitch it to a panel of space experts in June, with the goal of turning the app into a fully-functioning life-saving tool. The app would offer detailed maps of affected areas, distress signals for emergency services, and user-submitted information about potential hazards.

Sir Timothy O'Shea, a university leader, criticizes the proposed bill in Scotland's Higher Education Governance Bill, specifically the plan for directly elected chairs for university courts, as he believes it could be damaging, inconsistent, and incoherent, potentially affecting his university's independence, institutional autonomy, and the role of the rector. The Scottish government acknowledges the concerns, stating they will continue to listen to all views and work closely with the sector.

A Polish deli owner, originally from Ukraine, faces racial discrimination and expresses concerns about the potential impacts of Brexit on her business, including a weaker pound, and long-term viability due to integration challenges of a new generation.

Police in Dallas received an anonymous threat against law enforcement following the shooting of five white police officers by a black man, Micah Johnson, during a protest rally against police killings of black men. The police searched a nearby parking lot for a suspicious person but found no one. The US President, Barack Obama, condemned the Dallas killings but said the US is not as divided as suggested, and that Americans of all races were outraged by the killings. Johnson, who was killed during the assault, was a member of the US Army Reserve and had served in Afghanistan; bomb-making material, rifles, and a combat journal were found in his home. The Black Lives Matter organization condemned the Dallas shootings but said planned marches, including a "Weekend of Rage" in Philadelphia, would still go ahead.

Mr Abbott mentioned the possibility of accepting more Syrian asylum seekers but has not plans to boost overall refugee numbers. Several party members, including Frydenberg, Shorten, and various state premiers, have called for more action to help refugees, such as grants for temporary housing or increasing the number of refugee places. While the government emphasizes stopping refugees from reaching Australia by boat, state leaders such as Mike Baird of New South Wales push for further action and opening their doors to more refugees.

Nigel Farage claimed that Britain cannot meet its immigration targets as long as it remains in the EU and advocates for a return to normal levels of around 30,000 people per year. He stated that Britain's relationship with the European Union is a central issue in the election campaign.

Gareth Southgate, the former England defender, has been appointed as the permanent manager of the national team, succeeding Sam Allardyce, after impressing as interim boss. He has signed a reportedly £2m-a-year contract and his first competitive match will be a friendly against Germany in March. Southgate has experience in international football and development at St George's Park and has been praised by players and former officials for his tactical skills, leadership, and ability to connect with players. He led Middlesbrough for 151 matches between 2006 and 2009, but his 28.4% win percentage in the league is an unwanted record.

The FBI has ordered Apple to disable security software on an attacker's iPhone in a court case, but Apple has declined, with various tech leaders expressing support while some victims' lawyers advocate for potential cooperation in investigations. The iPhone belonged to Syed Rizwan Farook, one of the perpetrators of a mass shooting, and encryption protection concerns are among the reasons cited by tech leaders for supporting Apple's stance. John McAfee offered to unlock the iPhone for the FBI with the help of his team, with a promise to eat his shoe on television if they fail.
